These results highlight the value of noble gases as tracers of fluid evolution and permeability development in unconventional reservoir systems.

title: Toward coordinated water allocation in urban agglomerations under joint supply-demand uncertainty: A distributionally robust bi-level multi-objective framework
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Yan Tu, Qian Li, Yiqian Ding, Yongzheng Lu, Benjamin Lev
abstract: Coordinated water allocation is vital for urban agglomerations where high inter-city dependence amplifies systemic risks. However, traditional management faces strains from climate change and urbanization alongside conflicting interests across management levels. To this end, this study develops a distributionally robust bi-level multi-objective water allocation (DRBMWA) framework to facilitate coordination by integrating a Wasserstein-based distributionally robust representation of joint supply-demand uncertainty. The model features a bi-level multi-objective structure balancing economic cost, environmental load (COD), equity between cities (Gini coefficient), and systemic coordination, with lexicographic priorities (Living > Ecology > Production) reflecting social mandates. The original bi-level model is solved through a tractable single-level reformulation that embeds the lower-level lexicographic responses while preserving the hierarchical decision logic. Applied to the Shandong Peninsula urban agglomeration, results show that: (1) The DRO results reveal a robustness premium, as increasing the conservatism parameter α , which reflects the decision maker’s preference for uncertainty protection, from 1.0 to 1.5 raises the compromise cost by 34.88% while reducing the Gini coefficient from 0.034 to 0.018. (2) Under joint supply-demand stress, the deterministic compromise solution reaches a maximum city–sector shortage rate of 85.64 % , whereas the DRBMWA solution maintains sectoral shortage levels within a more controllable range. (3) Compared with the single-level model, the bi-level model reduces the maximum city shortage rate from 21.16% to 14.19% and strengthens the protection of living and ecological water, although at higher transfer cost and COD discharge. (4) Scenario analysis shows that worsening supply-demand conditions substantially increase transfer costs and weaken coordination performance, indicating a greater need for earlier transfer activation and larger fiscal reserves. These findings support annual quota setting, transfer planning, sectoral allocation, and contingency preparation under uncertain water availability.

title: Eutrophication reshapes lake-size scaling and amplifies the dominance of large lakes in regional CO 2 and CH 4 emissions across eastern China
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Hongtao Duan, Qitao Xiao, Tianci Qi, Juhua Luo
abstract: Accurate estimation of carbon dioxide (CO2) and methane (CH4) emissions from lakes is essential for refining the global carbon budget and understanding climatic feedback from inland waters. Previous lake carbon-flux estimates have often relied on field datasets dominated by small lakes, which exhibit high areal emission rates but may underestimate the contribution of large lakes. Satellite remote sensing offers an opportunity for spatially continuous monitoring of large and heterogeneous lake systems, yet robust methods for concurrently estimating CO2 and CH4 fluxes remain limited. Here, we developed polynomial regression models using Sentinel-3 satellite data to quantify dissolved CO2 and CH4 concentrations and their diffusive fluxes across 113 meso- to eutrophic lakes larger than 10 km2 in eastern China (R2: 0.50–0.78). By synthesizing multi-year midday observations under cloud-free conditions, we found that eutrophication reshaped conventional lake-size scaling of carbon emissions. Within the studied size range, smaller, highly productive lakes frequently acted as CO2 sinks, whereas larger lakes remained important CO2 sources. Nonetheless, the studied lakes acted regionally as net carbon sources because CH4 emissions offset the CO2 uptake in CO2-equivalent units. Large lakes (>100 km2), representing only 23% of lake number but 85% of total surface area, contributed 92% of regional CO2-equivalent diffusive efflux. These results suggest that eutrophication can fundamentally alter conventional lake-size scaling and should be explicitly considered in regional carbon upscaling. This study demonstrates the potential of satellite-based approaches for improving spatially explicit assessments of global carbon budgets, while emphasizing the need for broader validation and improved temporal representativeness.

title: Coexistence of Darcy and non-Darcy flows in deep limestone aquifers: insights from multi-scale imaging and pore-scale simulation
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Wenju Cheng, Chao Niu, Huiyong Yin, Lele Xiao, Qiang Sun, Chengwei Zhang, Songsong Cheng, Dabao Zeng
abstract: The deep Ordovician limestone aquifer in the Jungar coalfield has undergone intense physical dissolution and chemical filling, forming a highly heterogeneous and complex micro-pore-fracture multi-media system, which is a critical hazard-causing factor inducing mine water inrush. To reveal the seepage laws and micro-dynamic control mechanisms of the complex karst media, this study adopted multi-scale pore structure characterization techniques to finely and quantitatively extract the micro- and meso-scopic void topological structures of the limestone samples, and conducted pore-scale nonlinear dynamic simulations based on 3D digital core reconstruction. The results indicate that the porosity of the deep limestone media in the study area ranges from 2.1% to 4.2%, developing a highly heterogeneous coupled network of dissolution pores and micro-fractures. Among them, the micro-fracture system, with apertures mainly distributed between 14 and 60 μm, acts as the key hub connecting isolated dissolution pores, constituting the absolute dominant channel for fluid migration. The pore-scale simulations quantitatively revealed the significant characteristics of “multi-flow regime coexistence” within the complex and strongly heterogeneous media: in micro-dissolution pores and poorly connected regions, fluid momentum transfer is completely dominated by viscous resistance, manifesting as typical linear Darcy laminar flow; whereas in well-connected dominant micro-fracture channels and at locations with abrupt changes in pore-throat morphology, the fluid undergoes intense convergence and convective acceleration, leading to a significant increase in inertial forces. Driven by high hydraulic gradients, the flow regime within the dominant channels evolves into non-Darcy flow strongly controlled by local microstructures. From a micro-quantitative perspective, this study elucidates the coexistence mechanism of multiple flow regimes involving Darcy and non-Darcy flows in deep karst dual-media systems. The findings provide a solid micro-physical basis and novel insights for breaking through the single Darcy flow assumption, modifying macroscopic water inrush prediction models in mining areas, and formulating precise prevention and control strategies for coal mine floor water hazards.

title: Groundwater flow regimes and intrinsic vulnerability in a fractured bedrock aquifer: insights from hydrochemistry, isotopes, geophysics, and groundwater age
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Jaeyeon Kim, Ye Ji Kim, Chung-Mo Lee, Seho Hwang, Dong-Chan Koh, Yoon Yeol Yoon, Kang-Kun Lee, Hanna Choi
abstract: Intrinsic vulnerability in fractured bedrock aquifers is commonly evaluated using index-based approaches, yet these methods often underestimate the role of flow system architecture, recharge mechanisms, and groundwater renewal in controlling contaminant susceptibility. In structurally complex aquifers, vulnerability patterns are strongly controlled by heterogeneous flow paths and residence time distributions, which are not adequately represented by static approaches. This study integrates hydrochemistry, environmental isotopes (δ18O, δ2H, 87Sr/86Sr), tritium-based groundwater age modeling, multivariate statistical analysis, and geophysical investigations to constrain groundwater flow systems in a fractured bedrock aquifer in the Boeun region, Korea. Integration of these independent datasets reveals three distinct groundwater flow regimes: (i) a laterally dominated shallow system with strong surface connectivity, (ii) a vertically stratified mountain front recharge system with fracture-controlled deep circulation, and (iii) a rapidly renewed shallow system characterized by short residence times and diffuse recharge. The identified flow regimes provide a processed-based framework for interpreting intrinsic vulnerability. Despite groundwater quality index values indicating excellent water quality at present, DRASTIC results show moderate to high vulnerability associated with rapid recharge and structurally connected flow paths. This contrast demonstrates that intrinsic vulnerability is primarily controlled by recharge processes, groundwater flow systems, and renewal dynamics, rather than by static hydrogeological parameters alone. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating groundwater renewal dynamics, residence time structure, and flow system heterogeneity into vulnerability assessments of fractured aquifers.

title: Physics-informed machine learning of hyporheic exchange driven by channel blockage and riverbed morphodynamics
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Hang Li, Linlin Li, Defu Liu, Genguang Zhang, Jiahao Zou, Yu Lei, Canyong Li
abstract: Riverbed morphodynamic alterations induced by channel blockages, particularly those associated with large woody debris (LWD), play a critical role in modulating hyporheic exchange processes. However, most existing predictive approaches have not fully accounted for scour–deposition evolution, limiting the accuracy of hyporheic exchange flux (HEF) estimation. To address this, our study develops an enhanced physics-informed machine learning (PIML) framework to quantify the combined effects of hydraulic conditions, structural configuration, and riverbed morphology on hyporheic exchange dynamics. The computational framework generates 97 synthetic LWD-flow interaction cases, with six representative morphodynamic descriptors extracted to parameterize the resultant scour–deposition architecture. HEF was predicted through a hierarchical framework integrating empirical regressions, machine learning, and PIML, enabling adaptive estimation under varying data conditions. With morphodynamic descriptors available, both the empirical equation and ensemble learning models reproduced HEF with high accuracy (NSE ≈ 0.96); whereas using only initial flow–structure inputs reduced accuracy and the PIML approach, which incorporates the study-derived empirical flux equation, maintained higher performance (NSE = 0.79). SHAP analysis revealed that HEF is primarily governed by flow–morphology interactions and effective submergence ratio. Ensemble-based models, particularly Extra Trees and Gradient Boosting, demonstrated high predictive skill in capturing nonlinear morphodynamic responses. These results demonstrate that the hierarchical framework provides a unified and physically consistent strategy for predicting HEF across variable hydraulic–morphologic conditions.

title: Identification of spatiotemporal sensitivity of karst spring discharge to precipitation and evaporation: an LSTM–Transformer Decoder framework
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Xiping Yan, Meihong Ma, Yonghong Hao, Chunmei Ma, Wenrui Zhang, Qi Wang, Xiaogang Shi, Huiqing Hao, Xinyao Luo, Tianchyi Jim Yeh
abstract: Karst hydrological processes are driven by seasonal precipitation and evaporation and modulated by anthropogenic activities within highly heterogeneous aquifers. These processes produce spatiotemporally differentiated and magnitude-dependent responses that remain difficult to simulate and interpret. This study develops an LSTM–Transformer Decoders (LSTM–TDs) framework that links discharge-difference prediction with attention-based hydroclimatic sensitivity identification. To characterize discharge-change dynamics, the LSTM encodes historical first-order discharge differences into a discharge-change state, which then serves as the query for two spatiotemporal Transformer Decoder pathways separately attending to precipitation and evaporation inputs. The resulting attention structures are used to identify meteorological relevance across space, lag, and forcing magnitude. Applied to the Niangziguan Springs in North China, LSTM–TDs outperformed the evaluated benchmark models, with NSE = 0.85, RMSE = 0.34 m3/s, MAE = 0.26 m3/s, and MAPE = 3.88%. Relative to the non-differenced version, the discharge-difference design increased testing NSE from 0.79 to 0.85 and reduced MAPE by 19.8%. Attention-based sensitivity identification showed hydrologically plausible spatial and temporal patterns. Precipitation relevance was mainly concentrated in the main recharge–runoff area with relatively high groundwater levels, evaporation relevance was stronger in soil-moisture-rich areas, and dominant lags were consistent with cross-correlation-derived response times. The model-derived sensitivity turning points were approximately 42.0 mm for precipitation and 130.2 mm for evaporation, and their spatial variations were consistent with differences in infiltration partitioning, terrain-controlled redistribution, and aquifer storage conditions. These results indicate that the LSTM–TDs framework can support spring discharge prediction while providing interpretable diagnostics of hydroclimatic sensitivity in karst systems.

title: A refined reservoir evaporation loss estimation approach through improved wind function expression accuracy
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Cuihong Pan, Zengliang Luo, Lunche Wang, Zigeng Niu, Zushuai Wei, Ruijie Wang
abstract: Reservoir evaporation is a key component of the hydrological cycle, but its accurate estimation is hindered by complex reservoir geometry and spatially heterogeneous wind fields. Penman–based estimates of reservoir evaporation commonly represent wind direction using spatial averages over reservoir, neglecting shape effects and wind field heterogeneity, which introduces substantial uncertainty into evaporation estimates, especially for elongated reservoirs. This study proposes a reservoir–scale weighted wind direction method that incorporates reservoir geometry, spatial distribution features, while accounting for influencing factors. The method is applied to 6853 large reservoirs worldwide to estimate and analyze monthly evaporation during 1985–2021. The results showed that: (1) Compared with the mean wind direction method, weighted wind direction method yielded systematically lower wind direction variability ( Std weighted < Std mean , with negative mean relative bias and paired T–statistics), and showed better agreement with ground-based meteorological observations, with mean rRMSE and MAPE reduced by 0.29 and 25.43%, respectively. Accordingly, evaporation estimated using weighted wind direction method was more consistent with the TerraClimate, ERA5–Land and FLUXCOM evaporation products; (2) Differences in fetch length between the two methods were significantly negatively correlated with differences in evaporation (CC ≤ − 0.7), indicating that larger fetch length differences generally resulted in lower evaporation estimates derived from the weighted wind direction method, whereas similar fetch lengths between the two methods tended to produce relatively higher evaporation estimates from the weighted wind direction method; (3) During 1985–2021, the seasonality of monthly reservoir evaporation showed a clear spatial pattern, weakening from high latitudes in the Northern Hemisphere toward the Southern Hemisphere. Overall, 53.92% of reservoirs exhibited increasing trends, while 12.31% showed decreasing trends. These reservoirs were mainly used for irrigation and water supply, suggesting a potential link to intensified anthropogenic water use.

title: Decadal basin-wide nitrogen recovery and localized estuarine deterioration in the Bohai Sea revealed by physics-guided spatially adaptive machine learning
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Ruiteng Sun, Yuan Li, Longwen Fu, Kun Wang, Jing Yu, Fengshuo Yang, Yanfang Li, Xiaoguang Li, Shichao Tian, Youcai Liu, Dejuan Jiang, Yongming Luo
abstract: Excessive dissolved inorganic nitrogen (DIN) drives coastal eutrophication in semi-enclosed seas, yet retrieving this non-optically active nutrient in optically complex waters remains difficult, limiting decadal assessments of management progress. Here we reconstruct surface DIN across the Bohai Sea from 2013 to 2023 using a physics-guided, spatially adaptive machine-learning framework (GW-PGML-XGBoost) trained on 4,409 in-situ match-ups. The reconstruction reveals a decadal divergence: most of the basin recovered, while localized estuarine zones deteriorated. On the independent test set, the framework reproduced observations with R2 = 0.73 and RMSE = 0.094 mg L−1. Ablation attributed this skill to the coupled spatial and physical constraints, which raised R2 from 0.58 for standalone XGBoost. Prediction uncertainty, dominated by observational noise rather than model structure, was propagated into the trends, confirming that the divergence is robust to retrieval error. Sea surface salinity, sea surface height, and water depth were the dominant predictors, reflecting physical mixing and terrestrial loading. The climatology shows a persistent nearshore-high to offshore-low gradient and a seasonal cycle of summer minima and autumn–winter maxima. DIN declined significantly across the basin, tracking reductions in sewage, atmospheric, and agricultural nitrogen inputs. In Bohai Bay, the decline reached (−2.11 ± 1.17) × 10−3 mg L−1 yr−1 (p < 0.01), the steepest in the study area. Laizhou Bay, the most DIN-rich subregion, held steady at a high baseline (p = 0.39). In contrast, the localized estuarine increases coincided with intensified riverine inputs. Nutrient management in semi-enclosed seas should therefore shift from uniform annual-load reduction toward spatially precise, high-flow-season strategies.

title: Applications of artificial intelligence models in seawater intrusion: progress, challenges, and future directions
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Xiangdan Wang, Zhenxue Dai, Hao Wang
abstract: Seawater intrusion (SWI) poses a critical threat to global coastal freshwater security, exacerbated by the synergistic effects of anthropogenic groundwater extraction and climate-driven sea-level rise. While physics-based numerical models have traditionally underpinned aquifer management, their application is increasingly constrained by prohibitive computational costs and high-dimensional parameter uncertainty. This paper provides a critical review of the emerging application of artificial intelligence (AI) models in SWI management. We synthesize recent advancements across four key domains: salinity and water level prediction, real-time monitoring, dynamic vulnerability mapping, and multi-objective management strategies. The analysis demonstrates that deep learning architectures and data-driven surrogate models can effectively capture nonlinear temporal dynamics and accelerate optimization workflows compared with conventional methods. However, the operational maturity of these technologies remains hindered by significant bottlenecks, including heavy reliance on high-quality training data and the “black-box” nature of algorithms that lack physical interpretability and consistency with mass conservation laws. To address these limitations, we propose a strategic roadmap for future research focusing on the development of “grey-box” paradigms, in which hydrogeological knowledge and physical constraints are embedded into AI models. We further advocate integrating multi-source data fusion and adaptive real-time learning systems to bridge the gap between computational efficiency and hydrogeological reliability. This review offers a comprehensive framework for researchers and practitioners to leverage next-generation AI tools for resilient and sustainable coastal aquifer management.

title: Two new analytical models for constant rate pumping test in double-porosity multilayered confined systems: New Robin flow equation for aquitards
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Yexi Xiao, Ching-Sheng Huang
abstract: Accurate numerical solutions to aquitard flow equations derived based on an infinitesimal cubic require fine spatial discretization in aquitards. This study applies the divergence theorem of Gauss to derive a new Robin flow equation based on a finite-thickness element enabling no discretization in aquitards. Two analytical models are built for constant rate pumping test in a double-porosity three-layer confined system of two aquifers and one aquitard in between. One model applies the new Robin flow equation while the other applies a traditional aquitard flow equation. The semi-analytical solutions of the models are derived. The finite element solutions are also derived. Results suggest the new Robin flow equation is applicable within 5 % relative error in predicting drawdowns when quantitative conditions are met. The new Robin flow equation reduces to a new double-porosity lagging Robin boundary condition, and a typical Robin boundary condition in groundwater textbooks. Temporal aquifer drawdown can be triple-humped distribution with three flats due to the storage effects of the matrices in aquifers and aquitard. The finite element solution with the traditional aquitard flow equation can be accurate but requires about 10 6 nodes to discretize the aquifers and aquitard. The accurate finite element solution incorporating the new Robin flow equation requires only 2 , 002 nodes representing coarse square discretization in the aquifers and no discretization in the aquitard and takes 1 / 1503 of the computing time of obtaining the other accurate finite element solution with the traditional aquitard flow equation. The present solution applies to a field constant rate pumping test.

title: Coupled shallow-water hydrodynamics and reactive transport of emerging contaminants in unsteady flows
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Mengyun Wang, Mario Morales-Hernández, Pilar Brufau, Pilar García-Navarro
abstract: Emerging contaminants (ECs) pose persistent risks to aquatic ecosystems, yet their transport and fate in dynamic surface-water systems remain difficult to quantify because of trace concentrations and costly measurements. Existing shallow-water transport models often treat ECs as passive tracers or adopt simplified first-order decay formulations, limiting their ability to represent the integrated effects of hydrodynamic transport and physicochemical/biochemical reactions. To address this gap, this study develops one-dimensional (1D) and two-dimensional (2D) shallow-water reactive transport models for simulating the transport and fate of ECs in transient free-surface flows. The proposed framework integrates key EC-specific processes, including biodegradation, hydrolysis, photolysis, volatilization, bioconcentration/depuration, and sorption/desorption, within an advection–dispersion-reaction formulation coupled to shallow-water hydrodynamics. The models are first verified against reference solutions and then applied to a real flood event in the Ebro River using a hypothetical antibiotic release scenario. Results show that release timing strongly controls EC exposure patterns: for identical source loads, peak-flow releases produced lower concentration maxima because of stronger dilution and faster plume spreading, whereas recession-flow releases led to more persistent detectable concentrations. The 2D simulation also reveals flood-driven lateral transport from the main channel into inundated agricultural areas, highlighting the role of floodplain connectivity in shaping EC exposure under extreme events. To support high-resolution 2D applications, the model has been implemented on graphics processing units (GPUs), which reproduces the CPU results with significant computational saving. Overall, the study provides a computationally robust, efficient, and physically based framework for integrated simulation of EC transport and fate in dynamic shallow-water systems.

title: Physics-constrained neural network modeling of soil thermal conductivity curve across full saturation
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Yongwei Fu, Lingzao Zeng, Hu Zhou, Joshua Heitman, Tusheng Ren, Robert Horton
abstract: Accurate modeling of the soil thermal conductivity (λ) versus degree of saturation (S r) curve is essential for simulating coupled heat and water transfer in soils. Unlike point-wise estimates at selected water contents or at the saturated endpoint, a continuous λ(Sr) curve over the full saturation range is needed to represent soil heat-transfer behavior from dry to saturated conditions. Traditional theoretical models and standard data-driven approaches often struggle with generalization, overfit measurement noise, or yield physically implausible estimates when extrapolated beyond their training data. To address these limitations, this study introduces a Physics-Constrained Neural Network (PCNN) to learn a continuous, soil-specific λ(S r) curve over 0 ≤ S r ≤ 1 while applying established physical constraints. These embedded penalty terms promote monotonicity, nonlinear but smooth curve shapes, and physically realistic value ranges. The proposed PCNN is benchmarked against a purely data-driven Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) using a comprehensive dataset of 1846 measurements across 211 distinct soil samples. The MLP achieves lower error on the training dataset and a slightly lower testing RMSE, whereas the PCNN provides comparable testing accuracy while producing smoother and more physically consistent derivatives behavior. The PCNN maintains a robust testing-to-training RMSE ratio of 1.16 compared to the MLP’s ratio of 1.60, indicating stronger regularization rather than a large improvement in point-wise testing accuracy. Derivative-based analysis further shows that the MLP produces erratic, oscillatory curves and occasional physically impossible negative gradients, whereas the PCNN avoid negative derivatives in the diagnostic grid. These findings show that embedding physical constraints produces a continuous full-range λ(S r) function with more physically regular behavior than point-wise error minimization alone. By providing λ continuously as S r varies, the learned curve is intended as a constitutive input for simulations that traverse changing soil–water states. Future work should evaluate direct coupling of the learned relationship within larger-scale numerical heat-transfer simulations.

title: Simulation of soil water and nitrogen transport under drip fertigation using a dynamic infiltration boundary in HYDRUS
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Rui Chen, Peng Li, Weibin Zhang, Haitao Wang, Hui Wu, Xinjie Xu, Lei Zhang, Jian Wang
abstract: Accurate simulation of soil water and nitrogen transport under drip fertigation is crucial for optimizing water and fertilizer management. While the HYDRUS software is widely used for this purpose, the common approach of using a constant infiltration boundary often fails to represent the dynamic expansion of the surface ponding zone. This study developed a novel numerical approach to simulate soil water and nitrogen transport under drip fertigation by integrating a dynamic surface ponding radius model and parameterizing time-varying infiltration boundaries in HYDRUS-2D. The model was validated using a detailed dataset from a soil tank experiment with a silt loam soil. The simulation accuracy for soil water content and ammonium nitrogen (NH4 +-N) concentration was systematically evaluated under three infiltration boundary methods: a novel variable infiltration boundary method, a large constant infiltration boundary, and a small constant infiltration boundary with long fertigation duration. Results demonstrated that the variable infiltration boundary method significantly improved the prediction of soil water content, achieving high goodness-of-fit (NSE > 0.85, IA > 0.96, rP > 0.96) and low errors (MRE < 0.17, NRMSE < 0.15, PBIAS < 0.13). The optimal final infiltration boundary length was identified to be 5–10 cm larger than the maximum observed horizontal wetting front during the irrigation. For a constant infiltration boundary, its length should not be less than the soil horizontal wetting front at the end of irrigation and should not exceed this horizontal wetting front by more than 10 cm. Unlike soil water contents, NH4 +-N simulations were most accurate with a small constant infiltration boundary, highlighting a model limitation in assuming uniform solute concentration across the infiltration area, which likely does not reflect real-world solute accumulation beneath the emitter. This study concludes that a dynamically parameterized infiltration boundary enhances water flow simulation in soil under drip fertigation, but further refinement is needed for solute transport to account for spatial concentration gradients in the ponding zone.

title: Uncertainty propagation in water systems decision-making: A multi-parameter robustness framework
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Chao Tan, Xi Yang, Yulei Xie, Fenghua Huang, Min Qin, Zhihe Chen
abstract: Water systems are increasingly affected by hydrological variability, socio-economic change, and evolving management constraints, creating challenges for robust decision-making. Existing multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) approaches commonly rely on isolated parameter or weight perturbations and therefore provide limited insight into how multiple uncertainties jointly affect the robustness of decision outcomes. This study proposes a multi-parameter robustness framework to evaluate decision stability under interacting uncertainties. The framework combines objective weighting, coordinated perturbation of multiple criteria, and interval-based robustness diagnostics to assess the sensitivity of alternative rankings under large ensembles of disturbed scenarios. It is applied to two contrasting problems, namely reservoir flood-control operation at the Hongjiadu Reservoir and urban water supply planning in Zhengzhou. Results show that reservoir strategies emphasizing hydropower benefits tend to exhibit wider performance intervals and greater ranking volatility, whereas more risk-oriented strategies remain comparatively robust under changing conditions. In the urban water supply case, designs emphasizing a more balanced trade-off among investment, reliability, and long-term performance remain comparatively robust under concurrent disturbances. Across both cases, the results show that ranking robustness depends not only on the decision method itself, but also on the interaction between uncertainty structure and management objectives. The proposed framework provides a practical tool for identifying ranking vulnerabilities under bounded multi-parameter uncertainty and supports robustness-oriented planning for reservoir operation and urban water supply.

title: Ecohydrological trend detection in the Mobile Bay Watershed-AL using a rolling window Mann-Kendall test
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Henrique Haas, Musa Esit, Latif Kalin, John Lehrter
abstract: Detecting temporal variability in streamflow is critical for sustainable water management and ecological conservation. Traditional monotonic trend analysis methods, such as the Mann-Kendall (MK) test and Sen’s slope estimator, often fail to capture episodic or evolving trends embedded within hydrological time series. In this study, we apply a Rolling Window Mann-Kendall (RW-MK) method to identify “trends within trends” in streamflow metrics across the Mobile Bay watershed (MBW) in the southeastern United States. This method applies the MK test and Sen’s slope estimator across overlapping 30-year windows with a one-year lag, revealing subtle temporal variations that conventional approaches overlook. We assess annual, monthly, and ecologically relevant flow metrics derived using the Indicators of Hydrologic Alteration (IHA) framework. While traditional whole-period (monotonic) analysis showed no significant changes in mean annual flow, a rolling-window trend test uncovered significant declines in low flows (e.g., 1-day minimum flow at –1.94 m3/s/year for 1979–2008) and high flows (e.g., 7-day maximum flow at –70.91 m3/s/year for 1978–2007). Seasonal and percentile flow analyses further demonstrated spatiotemporal heterogeneity in trends, with significant decreases in both low and high percentile flows. Correlation analyses revealed that long-term declines in low-flow metrics were strongly associated with declining populations of oysters (Crassostrea virginica) and blue crabs (Callinectes sapidus), while spotted seatrout (Cynoscion nebulosus) exhibited opposite responses, highlighting potential ecological consequences of altered freshwater inflows in the Mobile Bay estuary. To facilitate broader application of the proposed methodology, we developed the open-source rwMK R package, which provides reproducible tools for rolling-window trend analysis and visualization. Our findings offer novel insights into the temporal variability of hydrological trends and support the use of moving window approaches in ecohydrological research.

title: Multi-objective optimization of water–sediment-ecology coordinated operation for cascade reservoirs in the Yellow River Basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Zhong-kai Feng, Liang Shen, Tie-sheng Guan, Ai-hua Long, Qin Xu, Xing Chen, Wen-jing Niu
abstract: Effective management of the water–sediment-ecology nexus in silt-laden rivers is a critical challenge for global hydrological sustainability. This study investigates the multi-objective coordinated operation of the Sanmenxia (SMX) and Xiaolangdi (XLD) cascade reservoirs in the Yellow River Basin, a system characterized by severe sedimentation and competing water demands. To address the complex, non-linear trade-offs between hydropower generation, sediment flushing, and downstream ecological protection, we implement an adaptive multi-objective JAYA algorithm (MOJAYA). The MOJAYA framework incorporates a two-population progressive optimization strategy and multidimensional adaptive search techniques to navigate the high-dimensional search space and stringent physical constraints inherent in multireservoir systems. Furthermore, a multivariate dependence analysis using Gaussian Copula functions is employed to quantify the inherent conflict intensity between the three objectives. Our results indicate a pervasive negative correlation across the operational landscape ( r = - 0.90 ), statistically validating the “high-water-head versus low-water-level” trade-off required for simultaneous hydropower and sediment management. Simulation results across representative wet, normal, and dry hydrological years demonstrate that the optimized schemes significantly outperform actual operations. Specifically, in wet years, power generation increases by 5% while the ecological water shortage rate is reduced from 2.01% to 0.84%. In dry years, the joint scheduling effectively mitigates the severe disruptions to ecological flow while maintaining energy reliability. This research provides a robust decision-support framework for balancing economic development and ecological integrity in complex, sediment-heavy river basins.

title: Variations in rainfall DOM as a driver of surface water concentration in the Chinese Loess Plateau-Qinling Mountains transition zone
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Caiqing Qin, Pinrong Ji, Ke Xu, Adrian M. Bass, Pan Zhang, Ji Chen, Yiping Wu
abstract: Wet deposition of dissolved organic matter (DOM) is important yet understudied for fluvial carbon cycling. To investigate rainwater DOM sources and their contributions to riverine systems in the Chinese Loess Plateau (CLP)-Qinling Mountains (QM) transition zone, this study captured 57 rainwater samples with varying rainfall intensities over one year, accompanying monthly surface water sampling from an adjacent river. Three major fluorescent DOM (FDOM) components were observed in rainwater, including a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon-like component (C1), a low-aromaticity humic-like component (C2), and a tryptophan-like proteinaceous component (C3). C1 dominated FDOM and exhibited seasonal variations, highlighting the importance of anthropogenic inputs, especially in summer. Higher aromaticity and humification in autumn and winter reflected the combined effects of anthropogenic inputs and photochemical processes. The results confirmed the influence of CLP dust on rainwater DOM, particularly during spring dust episodes. Backward trajectories revealed the contributions of air masses originating from dust source regions to increased particulate matter and associated organic compound inputs. The high-altitude QM acts as a geographical-climatic barrier regulating DOM transport. Rainwater-derived DOM contributed <1% to surface water directly, highlighting rainstorm-induced terrestrial runoff and in-stream biogeochemical processes for riverine DOM, consistent with the higher humification and aromaticity of riverine FDOM and their smaller seasonal fluctuation. The discrepancies in DOM between rainwater and surface river indicate different dominant source controls and processing pathways, while likely remaining linked through rainfall-runoff and post-precipitation transport. This study highlights the significance of underlying surface characteristics across CLP-QM regions in affecting rainwater DOM and its contribution to terrestrial riverine systems. Rainstorm-induced soil washing and runoff processes deserve attention for quantifying riverine DOM sources in the future.

title: A framework for analyzing spatial hydrological drought dependence based on extreme value theory and nonstationary copulas
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Yuqing Feng, Zhiyong Wu, Hai He, Zhenchen Liu, Yue Zhuo, Yangqian Li, Sergio M. Vicente–Serrano
abstract: Hydrological droughts are characterized by pronounced persistence and strong spatial dependence. Through river network connectivity, drought signals propagate across basins and frequently manifest as concurrent events in multiple regions. Their spatial dependence structures exhibit substantial regional heterogeneity and temporal evolution, posing methodological challenges for reliable risk assessment. This study proposes an integrated analytical framework that combines event-scale extreme value theory with nonstationary copulas to investigate hydrological drought dependence and concurrence risk. The framework characterizes the copula-based joint probability structure of upstream–downstream drought durations at the river network scale and explicitly accounts for its temporal nonstationarity. Hydrological drought events are first identified and matched at the event scale, and extreme samples are extracted using a Peaks Over Threshold approach. Time-varying parameters are then introduced to model both marginal extreme distributions and copula dependence parameters, enabling explicit representation of the temporal evolution of inter-site drought dependence structures. The framework is applied to the Yangtze River basin to systematically examine the spatiotemporal variation of hydrological drought dependence and concurrent drought probability under different upstream–downstream configurations. Results indicate that both the joint distribution structure and concurrent drought risk at the river network scale exhibit pronounced spatial heterogeneity and temporal nonstationarity, with no uniform evolutionary pattern across river reaches. Compared with stationary models, the proposed nonstationary framework more accurately captures changes in dependence structures and reveals temporal redistribution in the joint probability structure during upstream-to-downstream drought propagation. Overall, the proposed approach provides a statistically consistent and physically interpretable basis for assessing concurrent hydrological drought risk in large river networks under nonstationary conditions.

title: Improving reference evapotranspiration estimation by attention-enhanced autoencoders and hybrid neural networks under noisy chaotic conditions
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Sepideh Karimi, Mostafa Sadeghzadeh, Jalal Shiri, Pau Martí
abstract: The present study established a climate-adaptive Multi-Layer Perceptron-Self Attention (MLP-SA) framework for robust estimation of reference evapotranspiration (ETo) under noise-distorted conditions under different climatic conditions. The proposed model redefined noise-resilient ETo estimation through a climate-physics-informed two-stage architecture design: i) a denoising autoencoder (DAE) that first purifies noisy input data (meteorological variables, e.g. air temperature) by convolutional encoding–decoding, and ii) an MLP enhanced with a climate-adaptive self-attention mechanism, which dynamically recalibrated feature importance based on climate-specific physics. The proposed methodology was evaluated by using data from humid (north) and arid (south) regions. Despite statistical-based evaluation, the process-based hydrological analysis, as well as time persistence and hydrologically-significant error assessments, revealed the superiority of the proposed model under both climatic conditions. In the humid region, the model demonstrated a promising goodness-of-fit (R2 = 0.951; RMSE = 0.064 mm/day and MAE = 0.047 mm/day at 20% noise) by highlighting its dominance in suppressing high-frequency artifacts, outperforming hybrid models by more than 17% of R2. In the arid region, it provided optimal Lyapunov stability (λ = 0.531 at 40% noise, capturing 90.5% of observed chaotic dynamics), despite nonlinear degradation (ΔR2 = 0.108 from 0% to 40% noise). Climate-based assessment revealed that the humidity reduced feature interaction nonlinearity withlower SHAP distortion in the humid (|ΔSHAP|=0.151) compared to the arid (|ΔSHAP|=0.450) region. Furthermore, the attention mechanisms dynamically prioritized radiation-dominated hierarchies in the humid region (weight: 0.639), while multi-factorial weight assignment was detected in the arid region (Rs: 0.291, Ws: 0.290, RH: 0.263). The pure-attention architectures failed catastrophically (λ deficits exceeding 25%) due to inadequate chaos management. Further chaos-based assessment via the correlation dimension, phase reconstruction, and recurrence quantification analyses confirmed the promising ability of the proposed model in estimating ETo under different climatic conditions and noise levels.

title: Compound droughts as emergent outcomes of cascading drought propagation
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Prashant Prashant, Surendra Kumar Mishra, Anil Kumar Lohani, Vijay P. Singh
abstract: Compound drought is a complex phenomenon involving various components of the water cycle. Clarifying drought propagation pathways across meteorological, agricultural, and hydrological systems is therefore essential. However, the coupled and non-linear interactions among these drought types that give rise to compound drought conditions remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate compound drought as an emergent outcome of cascading drought propagation across Peninsular India. The proposed framework integrates drought propagation analyses to quantify the scale-dependent propagation of meteorological drought (MD) into agricultural drought (AD) and hydrological drought (HD). It also develops a trivariate copula-based Compound Peninsular India Drought Index (CPIDI) to characterize nonlinear joint drought occurrence and applies machine-learning (ML) emulation with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to interpret predictor contributions within the CPIDI emulation framework. MD, AD, and HD are characterized using the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) at multiple scales (3, 6, and 12 months), the Standardized Soil Moisture Index (SSI), and the Standardized Runoff Index (SRI) over 1980–2020. The drought-propagation hotspot analysis identified localized and pathway-dependent drought-prone catchments with priority hotspots concentrated over central India, parts of the eastern plateau, and selected southern catchments. CPIDI captured major historical drought years across SPEI scales. Furthermore, ML emulation reproduced CPIDI with high test performance and SHAP indicated that the CPIDI emulators relied mainly on SSI-1, SRI-1, and the scale-matched SPEI, confirming structural consistency within the CPIDI emulation framework. These findings provide empirical evidence that compound droughts emerge as outcomes of cascading drought propagation. Overall, this integrated framework provides a methodological foundation for future operational drought monitoring and assessment for water resources.

title: Enhancing river surface velocimetry through frequency-spatial feature fusion and confidence-based quality control
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Junjie Hao, Yuekun Ma, Yukun Li, Shuli Yu
abstract: Accurate measurement of river surface flow velocity is fundamental to hydrological monitoring and flood warning systems. In recent years, deep learning-based optical flow networks have shown great potential for river velocity estimation. However, existing approaches face two key challenges. First, models relying on spatial convolution are constrained by limited water surface texture. In weakly textured regions, insufficient local information leads to features lacking distinctiveness, resulting in multiple similar matching candidates during inter-frame feature correlation and thereby increasing optical flow estimation errors. Second, uneven tracer distribution and continuous surface deformation cause significant spatiotemporal variations in prediction reliability, yet existing evaluation methods apply indiscriminate averaging across spatial pixels and temporal frames, diluting high-quality estimates with low-quality results. This study proposes a wavelet-enhanced optical flow framework (WRAFT) built on the Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms (RAFT) architecture, addressing these challenges through frequency-spatial feature fusion and confidence-based quality control. For weakly textured regions, a frequency-domain branch extracts multi-scale flow information via wavelet transforms and fuses it with spatial features to enhance distinctiveness. For spatiotemporal reliability variations, a confidence module assesses prediction quality, selectively retaining high-reliability predictions while discarding low-quality results. Extensive evaluations based on seven public river datasets show that WRAFT consistently outperforms large-scale particle image velocimetry, space time image velocimetry, and baseline models under challenging conditions such as sparse tracers, specular reflections, and occlusions. The framework adapts effectively to diverse river scenarios with reduced reliance on site-specific parameter tuning, offering a practical solution for automated river monitoring.

title: Simultaneous aridification of soil moisture driven by anthropogenic activities in China’s loess critical zone
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Meng Ren, Yu Liu, Huiming Song, Qiufang Cai, Qiang Li, Changfeng Sun, Xiangyu Duan, Zekun Hu
abstract: The Chinese Loess Plateau (CLP), as China’s loess critical zone, exhibits pronounced sensitivity to soil moisture variations, which critically govern regional hydrological cycles and agro-ecological security. However, limited by scarcity of long-term in-situ soil moisture observations, the historical variations, trends and driving mechanisms of soil moisture in this region remain unclear, severely hindering accurate assessments of current and future ecological drought risks. Here, we present the first reconstructions of summer 0–10 cm soil moisture historical variations for the northeastern CLP (NEC) (1675–2012 CE) and southwestern CLP (SWC) (1556–2015 CE), based on tree-ring stable oxygen isotopes (δ18O). The study revealed a significant synchronous decline in soil moisture across both the NEC and SWC since the Industrial Revolution, with decline rates of 6.1 %/10a and 9.0 %/10a, respectively. Compared to the pre-industrial era, the soil moisture variation trends in both regions since the 1850s exhibited higher interdecadal coherence, along with significant increases in the frequency of extreme drought events.Attribution analysis of multi-model ensembles of Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) demonstrates that anthropogenic activities are the dominant drivers of the simultaneous aridification of soil moisture in the NEC and SWC since the 1850s.Concurrently, internal climate variability has synergistically amplified the soil moisture aridification trends and their spatial coherence on both interannual and decadal timescales. Our findings imply that regional soil moisture aridity will further worsen if global warming and anthropogenic activities intensify in the future.

title: Drivers, dynamics, and cascading effects of phased drought-flood abrupt alternation on basin water quality
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Zhenxiong Wang, Xiaoyan Bai, Jiefeng Wu, Yulei Xie, Zhenxing Zhang
abstract: With the intensification of global climate change, the frequency and intensity of drought-flood abrupt alternation (DFAA) events have been on the rise. However, current understanding of their cascading effects and dynamic impacts on river water quality remains insufficient. To this end, this study employed the Multiscale Multifactor Standardized DFAA Index (MSDFI) to identify monthly DFAA events from 2006 to 2018 in Southern China’s Lijiang River Basin. The events were categorized into two sub-events—Drought and Flood, and three periods: the Drought Development Period (DDP), the Drought Recovery Period (DRP), and the Flood Period (FP), for analyzing the dynamic changes and cascading effects on water quality (including pH, dissolved oxygen (DO), chemical oxygen demand (CODMn), and ammonia nitrogen (NH3-N)). The results indicated that: (Ⅰ) within DFAA events, pH and DO levels were elevated during droughts compared to normal conditions but decreased during floods, while the trend for CODMn was the opposite (lower during droughts and higher during floods). Besides, NH3-N concentrations exceeded normal levels in both the drought and flood periods. (Ⅱ) pH and DO showed linear variation patterns across different phases of DFAA events. CODMn and NH3-N demonstrated phase-integrated response patterns throughout the drought-to-flood (DTF) process, but their nonlinear characteristics became more pronounced during the flood-to-drought (FTD) processes. (Ⅲ) The alternation intensity of DTF events had a positive regulatory effect on CODMn levels. During FTD events, pH and DO levels were positively correlated with the alternation intensity, whereas NH3-N levels showed a negative correlation (p ≥ 0.05). (Ⅳ) pH and DO are primarily influenced by natural factors, while CODMn and NH3-N are regulated by deeper factors. This research provides valuable scientific insights into the dynamic changes in water quality and their driving forces during DFAA events, which is essential for formulating targeted water quality management strategies and enhancing the resilience of river ecosystems in the context of climate change.

title: Mapping temperate groundwater-dependent terrestrial ecosystems in Denmark
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): David Terpager Christiansen, Guy Schurgers, Rasmus Ejrnæs, Julian Koch
abstract: Groundwater-dependent Ecosystems (GDEs) are critical biodiversity hotspots and drought refugia that are driven by complex groundwater and ecological interactions. The detection of GDEs in temperate regions remains challenging due to weak phenological contrasts with surrounding vegetation. We developed a Positive-Unlabeled (PU) machine learning framework to detect temperate GDEs in Denmark using minimal input variables: two Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) variables derived from Sentinel-2 imagery, and Height Above Nearest Drainage. The approach exploits two NDVI signals: the drought-resilience of GDEs during dry summers (dry-season analogue), and their delayed spring green-up caused by waterlogged soils. Our model achieved 79% detection of field-mapped GDEs within Danish NATURA 2000 areas while identifying 7 times more potential GDE area (122.500 ha) and finds further 222.000 ha of GDEs in river valleys outside the monitored NATURA 2000 areas. Plausibility analysis using a Water table depth (WTD) dataset, and tree species dataset showed good agreement between labeled and predicted GDEs. Sensitivity analysis across different model parameterizations revealed predicted GDE coverage ranging from 22% to 65% of the study area, with true positive rates of 45% to 93%. The framework addresses key limitations in GDE mapping by requiring only positive training labels and few input variables. The model performs comparably to dryland GDE detection methods while operating without explicit dry season dynamics. These results establish a baseline for temperate GDE detection across regions, supporting land- and water-resources management, and compliance with environmental directives requiring GDE identification.

title: A decision-theoretic framework for probabilistic flood warnings
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Daniela Biondi, Ezio Todini
abstract: Early warning systems for weather-related hazards are critical tools for increasing societal resilience, but their effectiveness depends on reliability and ability to support decision-making in the face of uncertainty. While many operational contexts rely on expert judgment and predefined warning thresholds, decision-making processes rarely incorporate a formal assessment of the operational and economic impacts associated with the chosen actions. This study proposes a decision-theoretic approach for issuing flood warnings in Italy’s Sieve basin (Tuscany), integrating probabilistic precipitation forecasts from the national Civil Protection system with a statistical post-processing method to explicitly evaluate predictive uncertainty. The proposed framework introduces a loss function that adapts to multiple warning levels and accommodates different risk propensities (from risk-averse to risk-prone), effectively meeting the operational needs of diverse stakeholders. The system’s performance is evaluated by comparing a Bayesian decision scheme with one that explicitly accounts for precipitation forecast uncertainty, assessing cumulative economic costs against different baseline scenarios. Results demonstrate that adopting a Bayesian cost-based approach yields economic benefits and substantial improvements in the Relative Economic Value (REV). Furthermore, incorporating precipitation uncertainty drives the system toward more cost-effective warning strategies, reducing false alarms and expected losses.

title: Quantifying the effect of lateral seepage on the vertical saturated hydraulic conductivity of loess determined by the double-ring infiltration tests
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Xiaohu Jiang, Haijun Hu, Zhenghong Liu, Haotian Wang, Shuo Chen, Hui Wang, Yueting Huang
abstract: The double-ring infiltration test is widely used to determine the vertical saturated hydraulic conductivity (K sv) of soil in situ. While the lateral seepage inside the inner ring has been acknowledged, the effect of the lateral seepage on K sv and how to control this effect remains to be quantitatively investigated. In-situ double-ring infiltration tests, a test pit immersion test, and numerical simulations were conducted in this research to reliably obtain the K sv of Q 3 loess and quantify the effect of lateral seepage on the K sv determined by the double-ring infiltration tests. The determination of lateral seepage quantity was developed in numerical tests and the reliability was verified by comparing the proportion of total lateral seepage obtained by an inner diameter 60 cm × outer diameter 150 cm double-ring apparatus in-situ test using the water profile at the end of the test. In conventionally sized double-ring infiltration tests, real-time lateral seepage typically accounts for more than 50% or even 90% of the total flow during the steady infiltration stage, indicating that lateral seepage from the inner ring cannot be completely eliminated and may lead to an overestimation of the determined K sv. When real-time lateral seepage accounts for less than 55%, the total infiltration rate approximately equals the one-dimensional infiltration rate, i.e., the K sv determined by the double-ring infiltration test almost equals the true K sv value. It has been verified that this conclusion is universally applicable across other soil types. This study quantifies lateral seepage, previously considered merely a vague error source, and clarifies its mechanism of influence on the measurement of K sv and confirms that the equivalent frontal suction, which controls lateral seepage, is a key parameter governing the selection of double-ring dimensions. The findings provide a theoretical basis for optimizing the dimensions of double-ring infiltrometers and improving the accuracy of K sv determined by double-ring infiltration tests.

title: Precipitation water conversion rate variations and driving mechanisms in the Yangtze-Huang-Huai-Hai river basin over the past 60 years
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Haodong Deng, Yu Wang, Qingming Wang, Chaoqun Li, Fusheng Li, Dengming Yan, Xiaoxue Chen, Dongqing Zhang, Kai Hou, Benxing Lou, Lichuan Wang
abstract: Precipitation water conversion rate (PWCR) is a key indicator of the efficiency with which atmospheric vertically integrated water vapor content (IWV) is converted into precipitation. This study investigates the long-term variations and driving mechanisms of PWCR in the Yangtze-Huanghe-Huaihe-Haihe River (YHHH) basin, China, from 1956 to 2024. The results show that PWCR decreased significantly at a rate of −1.19%·dec−1, while IWV increased by 2.83 mm·dec−1 and precipitation decreased by −18.95 mm·dec−1. These opposite trends indicate that increasing atmospheric moisture did not translate into enhanced precipitation conversion. Seasonal analysis further reveals distinct mechanisms in summer and winter. In summer, PWCR is mainly controlled by precipitation changes jointly regulated by relative humidity (RH) and temperature. Higher RH favors precipitation formation, whereas warming may reduce conversion efficiency by increasing atmospheric moisture-holding capacity. In winter, PWCR is primarily governed by RH-mediated precipitation processes. Overall, the decline in PWCR reflects a weakening efficiency of atmospheric water vapor conversion under a warming and drying background. These findings improve understanding of water vapor–precipitation transformation in large monsoon-influenced basins and provide useful evidence for hydrological modeling and climate adaptation.

title: A procedure for geostatistical inversion incorporating a high-resolution initial hydraulic-conductivity field from travel time inversion
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Huiyang Qiu, Ning Luo, Yong Huang, Chao Zhuang, Xiaolan Hou, Walter A. Illman, Rui Hu
abstract: Hydraulic tomography (HT) has been proven as a robust approach to map subsurface heterogeneity through the joint inverse modeling of multiple pumping test data. A persistent difficulty is that GI can produce overly smooth or biased tomograms in data-sparse regions. TTI offers complementary information because it can efficiently recover a diffusivity (D) structure from early-time hydraulic responses. In this study, we propose a TTI-informed GI procedure. The procedure first estimates a D tomogram by TTI, converts that D tomogram into a heterogeneous hydraulic conductivity (K) field; which is utilized as initial K guess for GI. Three cases of HT analyses with various initial guesses are designed for a noise-free numerical case study, which are: (a) effective homogeneous K and Ss ; (b) zonation model results built by different structure information; (c) heterogeneous initial guess of K from TTI. The comparisons show that the proposed procedure is demonstrated effective for the Herten aquifer analogue, which is a well-characterized geological database in Germany. It has outstanding performance similar to a scenario of integrating a zonation model with accurate geological information. This study highlights that the TTI results with acceptable quality can contribute to improving the performance of GI in data sparse areas, especially when geological information is not available.

title: Impact of reservoir storage on propagation from meteorological to hydrological drought
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Ajay Gupta, Manoj Kumar Jain, Rajendra Prasad Pandey, David M. Hannah
abstract: Reservoirs are central to moderating and mitigating drought, yet their influence on drought propagation through socio–hydrological systems remains under–examined. This study quantifies how reservoir storage shapes the progression of meteorological, agricultural, reservoir, and streamflow droughts across 11 major reservoirs in the semi–arid Krishna River Basin, India (2000–2019). Using the SPEI, SSMI, SRSI, and SSI indices, we estimate initiation, peak, and termination lags at multiple timescales and thresholds. Reservoir influence is further assessed using the Downstreamness concept to capture upstream–downstream hydrological connectivity. Results show that drought propagation varies markedly across indices due to contrasting system response times. Meteorological–to–agricultural drought propagates rapidly at short timescales, whereas agricultural–to–reservoir and reservoir–to–streamflow droughts exhibit longer delays linked to reservoir buffering. Termination is most variable for agricultural–to–reservoir drought and shortest for reservoir–to–streamflow drought, reflecting rapid downstream recovery once reservoirs refill. Upstream–downstream analysis reveals that mild and moderate upstream reservoir droughts rarely propagate, but severe upstream droughts consistently transmit downstream, with longer duration, greater severity, and delayed onset. Downstreamness dynamics further show shifting patterns of water retention over the drought cycle, underscoring the importance of hydrological connectivity in shaping drought outcomes. These findings provide actionable insights for basin–scale water management, highlighting the need to incorporate reservoir connectivity and drought–severity thresholds into drought mitigation strategies. The approach offers transferable value for other semi–arid basins facing similar multi–stage drought propagation challenges.

title: Learning geometry-aware streamflow forecast models from a large-scale river graph dataset
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Alexander Y. Sun, Albert A. Sun
abstract: Streamflow forecasting is a central component of hydrological modeling, providing critical decision support to a wide range of water resources applications. In recent years, numerous data-driven and hybrid machine learning (ML) methods have been introduced, yet their predictive capacity depends critically on how effectively complex spatial and temporal processes across multiple scales are represented. Here we investigate the feasibility of incorporating river network geometry as a structural constraint in training basin-agnostic streamflow forecasting models. We curate a large-scale graph dataset comprising more than 500 U.S. basin networks, nearly 100,000 river nodes, and approximately six billion data points. River graphs are constructed from high-resolution hydrofabric layers. Message-passing graph neural network (GNN) models are developed to learn generalizable latent representations of river network dynamics, using inputs/outputs of the U.S. National Water Model (NWM). Results demonstrate that a single GNN may be pretrained to approximate the NWM streamflow dynamics reasonably well, with the best-performing GNN model achieving a median Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) exceeding 0.8 across all river network nodes and 0.96 at basin outlet nodes for 3-hour-ahead forecasting. The pretrained GNN model exhibits robust performance when tested on holdout basins outside the range of training basins. Furthermore, fine-tuning the pretrained model using gauge observations reduces model biases inherited from the NWM, further improving predictive performance. These findings highlight the potential of geometry-aware GNNs as a new class of scalable hydrological ML models.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and propagation of GNSS-derived PWV-based meteorological and soil moisture drought: a case study of the contiguous United States (2003–2022)
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Weiao Yong, Xiaolei Wang, Hao Yang, Jinsheng Tu
abstract: Accurate drought characterization requires indicators that can capture atmospheric and terrestrial processes over multiple scales. While traditional drought indices derived from satellite and reanalysis data are well established, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)-derived precipitable water vapor (PWV) offers a high-temporal-resolution, all-weather alternative that remains underutilized in current drought monitoring frameworks. In addition, understanding the propagation from meteorological drought (MD) to soil moisture drought (SMD) is essential for revealing drought evolution mechanisms. In this study, a novel application of GNSS PWV, in combination with precipitation, was used to construct a Standardized Precipitation Conversion Index (SPCI) for characterizing meteorological droughts across the contiguous United States (CONUS) during 2003–2022, while SMD were quantified using the Standardized Soil Moisture Index (SSMI) to further investigate drought propagation dynamics. Results revealed that the SPCI demonstrates strong agreement with SPI and SPEI across multiple timescales. MD showed a tendency toward intensification in 50.19% of the CONUS, while only 4.07% showed significant trends (p < 0.05), with drought events characterized by high frequency and long durations. SMD exhibited even greater intensification, with 59.56% of the CONUS showing worsening drought conditions, with 40.53% showing significant trends (p < 0.05), and events tending to be more prolonged and severe. Leveraging both indices, a spatiotemporal analysis of drought propagation from MD to SMD was conducted. A widespread and rapid propagation was identified, with approximately 73.80% of the region exhibiting a propagation time within 0–1 month. The fastest propagation (around 0.1 month) occurred in the Southwest and West climate regions, while arid and humid zones showed longer propagation durations than semi-arid and semi-humid regions. To further understand the underlying mechanisms, driver attribution analysis was performed. Precipitation was identified as the dominant driver for both MD and SMD, while dew point temperature emerged as an important secondary factor, particularly for SMD development in the southwestern CONUS. These findings suggest that incorporating GNSS-derived PWV provides additional atmospheric moisture information that improves the understanding of drought characteristics and their propagation from the atmosphere to the land surface, supporting improved drought monitoring and early warning.

title: Probabilistic prediction of thermal plumes from groundwater heat pump wells using ANN surrogate modeling
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Alberto Previati, Valerio Silvestri, Paolo Frattini, Giovanni Crosta
abstract: Groundwater heat pumps (GWHPs) represent an efficient solution for urban heating and cooling, but their widespread adoption raises concerns about thermal interference and long-term sustainability in densely exploited aquifers. This study presents a novel data-driven framework for predicting GWHP thermal plumes to support risk-based groundwater thermal resource management. A fully connected neural network (FCNN) surrogate model was developed and trained on 4,500 3D finite-element heat transport simulations, spanning a wide range of hydrogeological conditions and GWHP operational scenarios, including variable injection rates and combined heating/cooling operations. The surrogate reproduces numerical results with high accuracy, achieving a mean absolute percentage error of 5% in predicting the extent of the ±1°C thermal perturbation isotherm after 20 years of operation. The robustness and generalization capability of the model were assessed through a bootstrapping testing procedure with scenario-based data splitting. The model is embedded in a Monte Carlo framework to explicitly account for uncertainty in hydrogeological parameters and system operation, enabling probabilistic mapping of thermal perturbation. The methodology is applied at the city scale in Milan (Italy), producing probability maps of thermal interference for existing GWHP installations. Furthermore, the approach is extended to resource planning by estimating the maximum extractable groundwater volume for new installations while limiting temperature perturbations at existing wells to ±1°C. The proposed framework bridges the gap between analytical screening tools and computationally intensive numerical models, providing a scalable and robust decision-support tool for sustainable shallow geothermal energy management in urban aquifers.

title: Photo-dependent processes and their effect on the CO 2 dynamics in high-altitude wetlands
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Josefa Rojas-Araya, Gino Vera, Francisco Gracia, Alberto de la Fuente, Ana L. Prieto
abstract: High-altitude wetlands in South America, or “salares,” are found in the central depression of the closed catchments in the Andean Altiplano region of Chile, Bolivia, Peru, and Argentina. Formed by groundwater upwelling and surface evaporation, salares are subjected to severe environmental conditions and host mineralogically rich soils dominated by metallic oxides, including TiO2. This study combines field observations of CO2 fluxes across the air–water interface (AWI), water quality parameters, soil mineralogy composition, and phenomenological models to characterize the transport and reactivity of CO2 at the Salar del Huasco (Chile). Eddy-covariance measurements at Huasco’s Water and adjacent Desert sites show that CO2 uptake is tightly coupled to shortwave solar radiation and humidity, a pattern inconsistent with benthic photosynthesis alone and indicative of an uncharacterized photo-dependent sink. As a first step toward characterizing potential photo-dependent processes, the photocatalytic reduction of CO2 to CH4 and the deposition of carbonates were evaluated in controlled laboratory experiments.Although field data reveal net CO2 uptake of up to 4 g CO2 m−2 d−1 during austral spring, photocatalytic reduction and carbonate formation were not confirmed under laboratory conditions. Nevertheless, a first-order transport–reaction model reproduced observed fluxes across three independent field campaigns (NSE = 0.73–0.78, ρ = 0.89–0.92), with a single set of photochemical parameters transferable between Huasco’s Water and Desert sites. This study provides previously overlooked insights into the role of photo-dependent processes in high-altitude wetlands; however, future work should identify specific photo-dependent processes and their spatial/seasonal contributions to the CO2 dynamics of the Salar del Huasco.

title: Multi-modal dual-target spatio-temporal graph learning for regional evapotranspiration estimation
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Kwame Adutwum Gyamfi, Eun-Sung Chung
abstract: Accurate evapotranspiration (ET) estimation remains challenging because physically based formulas rely on simplifying assumptions, whereas satellite products contain retrieval uncertainty. We develop a multi-modal dual-encoder, dual-target spatio-temporal graph neural network for regional ET estimation over the Korean Peninsula. The framework treats meteorological forcing and MODIS-derived surface descriptors as heterogeneous but complementary modes. A hybrid graph represents geographic-distance and inter-station-correlation structure, modality-specific graph encoders and a recurrent temporal encoder capture spatio-temporal dependence, and a learnable gate fuses climate and satellite representations while quantifying their relative contributions. The model is trained jointly against MODIS ET and FAO-56 Penman–Monteith reference ET (PM ET0), combining satellite-observed actual ET with meteorological evaporative demand. On the holdout test set, the model achieved MAE/RMSE/ R 2 of 2.197/3.503/0.883 for MODIS ET and 0.473/0.615/0.999 for PM ET0. Relative to a graph-free CNN + LSTM dual-head baseline, MAE decreased by 33.3% for MODIS ET and 39.0% for PM ET0. Component ablation showed that the full multi-modal dual-target configuration reduced joint MAE by 40.0% and RMSE by 38.6% relative to the single-encoder MODIS variant. Gate analysis showed that climate and satellite contributions vary by season and input position, making the fusion interpretable rather than fixed. MC-dropout uncertainty with isotonic calibration achieved PICP90 of 0.895 and 0.899 for MODIS ET and PM ET0, respectively. Multi-horizon tests retained seasonal predictability up to 12 months.

title: Monitoring-constrained GPR inversion reveals profile-scale hydrothermal heterogeneity in a retrogressive thaw slump
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Shunshun Qi, Fei Wang, Guoyu Li, Wei Ma, Dun Chen, Fujun Niu, Mingtang Chai, Yougang Yang, Qingsong Du, Kai Gao, Yapeng Cao, Jiawei Yang
abstract: Retrogressive thaw slumps (RTSs) rapidly reshape microtopography and near-surface structure on permafrost hillslopes, altering infiltration pathways, hillslope–channel hydrologic connectivity, and subsurface heat–water exchange. However, point observations remain insufficient to resolve hydrothermal heterogeneity and near-zero temperature-zone processes at the profile scale. Here, using a representative RTS site in the northeastern Qinghai–Tibet Plateau (QTP), we develop a monitoring-constrained ground-penetrating radar (GPR) framework for profile-scale hydrothermal inversion. Stratified monitoring data from an undisturbed reference area are used to establish relationships among relative permittivity, temperature, and volumetric water content, which are then applied to multi-temporal GPR profiles to reconstruct two-dimensional temperature and water-content fields. The temperature inversion retains high accuracy near phase transition, with an RMSE of 0.219 °C. The reconstructed profiles reveal clear seasonal contrasts in the near-zero temperature zone, with areal proportions of 0.482–0.485 in early July and 0.738–0.744 in late October. Among the late-October profiles, the mean depth of the 0 °C isotherm varies little, whereas its lateral roughness ranges from 0.114 to 0.135 m, indicating stronger lateral thermal heterogeneity. At the slump head, shallow mean water content differs little among profiles, but wet-zone occupancy differs by 14.7 percentage points at a water-content threshold of 0.35 and nearly doubles at 0.40. These results show that structural metrics provide more sensitive profile-scale constraints for interpreting subsurface water redistribution and heat-transfer processes under RTS disturbance, thereby providing a useful reference for assessing hydrothermal reorganization in degrading permafrost landscapes.

title: Cascade structure and event-level attribution of three-dimensional compound drought–heat events in China: contrasting meteorological and agricultural systems
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Ben Niu, Yi Li, Shasha Han, Jinxuan Zhao, Darrell W.S. Tang, David M. Hannah
abstract: Compound drought–heat events are among the most damaging climate extremes because concurrent water deficits and heat stress amplify impacts on ecosystems and agriculture. Here, we investigated compound drought–heat events across China during 1961–2023 using monthly 0.25° × 0.25° gridded CN05.1 and GLDAS datasets. Non-stationary drought and heat indices were first developed using GAMLSS to represent time-varying marginal distributions, and Copula models were then used to derive meteorological and agricultural compound drought–heat indices. A spatial-overlap-constrained three-dimensional event-identification framework was applied to characterize event evolution, cascade structure, and key spatiotemporal features, and explainable machine-learning models were used to diagnose dominant event-level predictors. Results showed that compound drought–heat events were more concentrated in the upper tails of area–severity distributions than single drought or heat events, especially in the meteorological system. Since the 1990 s, both systems intensified, but meteorological events showed higher intensity, peak, and migration, whereas agricultural events persisted longer once established.
