These findings have implications for crayfish health and for overall ecosystem functioning in environments known for the occurrence of MC-LR.

title: An advanced hydrological approach for the characterization of the Water Scarcity Footprint at the sub-basin level
description: Publication date: 10 September 2026 Source: Science of The Total Environment, Volume 1047 Author(s): Niccolò Renzi, Benedetto Rugani, Daniele Penna, Tommaso Pacetti, Enrica Caporali, Elena Bresci, Giulio Castelli
abstract: ISO 14046:2014 is nowadays the international standard for measuring the Water Footprint (WF) of products, processes, and organizations, following a life cycle approach. The Available Water Remaining (AWARE) is an ISO 14046-compliant characterization model to measure the WF characterization factors (CFs) at national and sub-national levels considering only the quantity aspect of the impact, named Water Scarcity Footprint (WSF). Despite being established on international consensus, AWARE is calculated with global water balance models and does not entail data of hydrological dynamics at high spatial resolution. Thus, the resulting WSF values may be inaccurate for local studies. We calculate sub-regional CFs at hyper-resolution (sub-basin scale) to highlight water shortages that are not visible using current methods and improve the reliability of WSF of products and processes. Hydrological information (i.e., water availability) was retrieved from the Italian national water balance model with 1 km spatial resolution (BIGBANG 7.0), and water consumption time series (2012−2021) were obtained at the municipality level. Results show that the recalculated CF for Tuscany (= 41.8 m3 world equiv. m−3) is ∼26% higher than the original AWARE's CF, suggesting that the method is not able to capture the variability of water dynamics at the sub-basin level. WSF results for three representative crops (tomato, apple and corn) are influenced by the new CFs, increasing between 50% and 100%. The proposed approach can improve the reliability of WSF assessments and can be extended to the entire Italian territory and other territories in the world.

title: Irrigation management and groundwater recharge in Mediterranean intermontane basins: a multi-method evaluation of agricultural controls and interbasin variability
description: Publication date: 10 September 2026 Source: Science of The Total Environment, Volume 1047 Author(s): Bisrat Ayalew Yifru, Leland Scantlebury, Shubham Tiwari, Claire Kouba, Laura Foglia, Thomas Harter
abstract: Groundwater recharge in irrigated agricultural landscapes and surrounding watersheds is critical for sustainable water management and environmental flows. In irrigated Mediterranean regions, quantifying this process is complicated by substantial interannual and spatial variability in precipitation, irrigation practices, and evapotranspiration (ET), which introduces significant uncertainty. Here, we assess field-scale spatiotemporal variability in potential and actual contributions to aquifer replenishment across Mediterranean intermontane irrigated basins. Potential estimates were derived from a remote sensing ET water-balance residual (RSET-WB) and soil water balance modeling (SWBM), whereas the actual component was inferred from groundwater-level fluctuations using the water-table fluctuation method (WTFM). Results reveal strong spatial and crop-specific contrasts among basins and fields. In SWBM, irrigation-season variability was primarily associated with soil available water storage (AWS) and crop type, whereas non-irrigation season patterns were explained largely by interbasin differences in wet-season precipitation. Crop-specific patterns differed between methods, with alfalfa dominating RSET-WB residual estimates and grain and pasture lands showing greater SWBM-derived dry-season deep percolation below the root zone. Within SWBM, low-AWS fields also showed enhanced growing-season drainage. WTFM estimates indicated relatively balanced water table recharge between wet and dry seasons across most basins, contrasting with the wet-season dominance shown by RSET-WB and SWBM. Long-term averages (2008–2023) from RSET-WB and SWBM suggest that the dry season accounted for about 29–34% of annual potential recharge, while the wet-season fraction ranged from 54% to 78% of precipitation. Collectively, these findings underscore that irrigation return flow and late-season precipitation are critical to sustaining groundwater potential recharge in Mediterranean agricultural lands, supporting managed aquifer recharge strategies such as early- or off-season irrigation in low-AWS pasture grasslands.

title: Life cycle assessment as a tool to improve the environmental sustainability of urban forest management - An Italian case study
description: Publication date: 10 September 2026 Source: Science of The Total Environment, Volume 1047 Author(s): Roberto Petrucci, Desirée Muscas, Fabio Orlandi, Luigi Torre, Livia Bonciarelli, Marco Fornaciari
abstract: Urban trees play a crucial role in delivering ecosystem services (ES), such as reducing PM10 concentrations, and acting as carbon sinks to combat the climate crisis. While previous life cycle assessment (LCA) studies have highlighted how tree environmental performance largely depends on the species, transforming Urban Forests (UF) composition is a slow, long-term process. Therefore, this study relies on the lessons learnt from the Life Clivut project (LIFE18 GIC/IT/001217) in Mediterranean UF. Specifically, it aims to identify the processes within conventional urban tree management that exert the greatest environmental impact, enabling targeted intervention on pollution hotspots to achieve meaningful short-term reductions in overall environmental burdens. The LCA study, conducted using SimaPro 9.6.0 software, focuses on the city of Perugia (Italy) to assess the environmental benefits of implementing Clivut Best Practices. By analysing the most promising strategies tested in Clivut pilot cities, the study designs a “Future scenario” to further improve the municipal environmental performance by adopting electric tools in UF management. The study is based on ReCiPe 2016 Endpoint (H) and Midpoint (H) LCA impact assessment methods over a 70-year timeframe. Results indicate that the most significant improvements in environmental performance occur between the benchmark scenario and the implementation of Clivut Best Practices (21%), while shifting to the Future scenario determines only a 0.8% improvement. Notably, utilising chipped wood residues as mulch proves to be environmentally beneficial only on large volumes of pruning residues (>2554 Kg). However, the use of electric brush cutters and power saws would reduce the environmental impact of the tools by −2% and − 66%, respectively, while it would be detrimental in the case of car-driven green monitoring activities (+29%).

title: Climate extremes, WASH deficits, and infectious diseases in the Brazilian Amazon: Insights from explainable machine learning (2010−2022)
description: Publication date: 10 September 2026 Source: Science of The Total Environment, Volume 1047 Author(s): Ana Karoline Duarte dos Santos Sá, Marco Valerio Jansen Cutrim, Rafael Diego Barbosa Soares, Quedyane Silva da Cruz, Andrea Christina Gomes de Azevedo Cutrim, Yago Bruno Silveira Nunes, Paulo Henrique Rocha Aride, Jeniffer Hachiley de Sousa Torquato, Antonio Ronnilson Dias Carneiro Sá
abstract: Infectious diseases transmitted through environmentally mediated faecal–oral pathways and climate-sensitive vector-borne routes remain major public health challenges in the Brazilian Amazon, where sanitation deficits interact with hydroclimatic variability. This study investigated how ENSO-related climate variability, sanitation conditions, and socioenvironmental factors jointly influence disease incidence across seven Amazonian states from 2010 to 2022. Epidemiological, climatic, and socioeconomic datasets were integrated using statistical models and explainable machine learning approaches. Disease incidence exhibited strong heterogeneity across transmission pathways. Climate was the dominant predictive domain for faecal–oral, contact-related, and arboviral diseases (mean SHAP up to 0.871), whereas spatial structure dominated protozoan vector-borne diseases and the combined model (up to 0.628). At the variable level, contributions were concentrated in a limited set of predictors, particularly state effects (up to 0.401) and key climatic variables, including temperature and lagged humidity and rainfall. Lagged climatic variables (t − 1) contributed substantially to model performance, indicating delayed responses to environmental variability. Generalized additive models showed high explanatory capacity, with explained deviance ranging from 68.2% to 94.9% across disease groups. Ensemble models outperformed conventional approaches, capturing nonlinear relationships among predictors. Overall, climate variability acted as a modulating factor within a broader system of structural vulnerability, rather than as an isolated driver. These findings support integrated strategies combining sanitation improvements, climate-informed early warning systems, and spatially targeted public health interventions.

title: Equilibrium iridium isotope fractionation in metals, silicates, oxides, sulfides, and halides: insights from first-principles calculations of mass-dependent and nuclear-volume effects
description: Publication date: 1 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 428 Author(s): Feixiang Liu, Yining Zhang, Edwin A. Schauble, Alexander P.W. Sedlak, Caihong Gao, Xiaobin Cao, Yun Liu, Qi Liu
abstract: Stable iridium isotopes (191Ir, 193Ir) offer novel potential for investigating geological processes, yet their application in natural systems remains hindered by poorly constrained fractionation behaviors. To establish a predictive framework, we present the systematic first-principles calculations of equilibrium Ir isotope fractionation (273.15–5000 K) for Ir-bearing phases, concurrently evaluating mass-dependent and nuclear volume effects. Our results demonstrate that mass-dependent fractionation dominates over nuclear volume fractionation in most species, but the contribution of latter to the overall isotope fractionation increases with increasing temperature. Critically, we establish a systematic enrichment sequence for 193Ir during igneous processes: metallic Ir (Ir0) < sulfides (Ir3+, Ir4+) < silicates (Ir1+, Ir2+) and halides (Ir3+, Ir4+) < oxides (Ir2+, Ir3+, Ir4+). Beyond conventional factors (temperature, oxidation state, bond length, and electron density), we further identify the significance of bonding atom properties (electronegativity, ionic radius, effective ionic charge), non-bonded interactions, and structural constraints in influencing equilibrium isotope fractionation. This work provides a fundamental understanding of Ir isotope fractionation behaviors, enabling reliable interpretation of natural isotopic variations and advancing Ir isotopes as tracers for geological processes.

title: The behavior of rubidium during evaporation: evidence from element and isotope compositions of tektites
description: Publication date: 1 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 428 Author(s): Xi Deng, Jinting Kang, Pei-Yi Li, Yun Jiang, Haolan Tang, Yang Xiao, Fang Huang
abstract: Rubidium (Rb) is a moderately volatile element (MVE), and its isotopic system has been widely applied to constrain evaporation and condensation processes during solar nebular evolution and planetary accretion. Tektites, natural glasses formed by the rapid melting and quenching of terrestrial crustal materials during hypervelocity impacts of extraterrestrial bodies, serve as critical geological archives for quantifying impact-driven volatile loss, particularly for MVE. Here, we report high-precision Rb isotopic data for tektites from the Australasian, North American, Central European, and Ivory Coast strewn fields, obtained via both micro-drilling (in-situ) and bulk dissolution analyses. In-situ edge–center–edge profile analyses of three australasites reveal negligible Rb concentration variations (<10%) and remarkable isotopic homogeneity, with δ87Rb ranging from –0.16 ± 0.01‰ to –0.09 ± 0.03‰ (2SD). The absence of resolvable elemental or isotopic zoning across these profiles rules out diffusion-limited evaporation as the dominant control on Rb behavior during tektite formation. Bulk δ87Rb for all analyzed tektites range from –0.22 ± 0.05‰ to –0.12 ± 0.03‰, yielding a mean of –0.16 ± 0.06‰ (2SD, n = 14). This uniformity indicates no resolvable Rb isotopic fractionation and is consistent with the composition of the upper continental crust (δ87Rb = –0.14 ± 0.01‰). To further evaluate the volatility behavior of MVE under Earth-surface conditions, we perform thermodynamic modeling at ambient atmospheric pressure and oxidizing conditions. The model predicts a volatility sequence of Zn ≫ Rb ≥ K, consistent with the well-documented large Zn isotopic fractionations in tektites and the absence of measurable isotopic shifts in Rb and K. Collectively, these results may imply that Rb isotope fractionation is effectively suppressed during impact-induced evaporation under the oxidized, near-surface conditions of Earth.

title: Iron isotope compositions of sediment with depth-dependent iron reduction in a temperate eutrophic freshwater lake
description: Publication date: 15 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 427 Author(s): Chenhui Wei, Juan Liu, Xi Yang, Tao Huang, Changchun Huang, Shu Tao, Dongqiang Zhu
abstract: Pathway-dependent iron isotope fractionation is a powerful tool for evaluating iron biogeochemical cycle. Lake sediments host complex iron redox transformations, yet very few iron isotope investigations have been performed on lake sediments. Here, we combined high depth-resolution multi-biogeochemical analyses with stable iron isotope measurements to investigate a sediment core (21 cm) from Baiyangdian, a temperate eutrophic freshwater lake in North China. The excess 210Pb analysis indicated an undisturbed sedimentary record in the lake. In the top 4 cm, sulfide accumulated in the porewaters and the reactive iron was mainly present as iron sulfides (51–86%), indicating that Fe(III) (oxyhydr)oxides were primarily reduced by sulfide. Accordingly, the δ56Fe values of sorbed Fe(II) plus tightly-bound Fe(II) (mostly FeS with little FeCO3) gradually decreased from −0.21 ± 0.06‰ to −0.95 ± 0.10‰ with depth. Meanwhile, the isotope fractionation between Fe(III) (oxyhydr)oxides and sorbed Fe(II) plus tightly-bound Fe(II) ranged from 1.02 ± 0.10‰ to 1.60 ± 0.10‰. Due to the great extent of pyritization, pyrite exhibited relatively heavy δ56Fe values (−0.32 ± 0.04‰ to 0 ± 0.09‰) within the 1–4 cm layer. Below 4 cm depth, microbial iron reduction became dominant in the absence of sulfide. Fe2+ concentrations in the porewaters gradually increased with depth, and non-sulfur-bound iron species dominated the reactive iron pool (67–94%). The sorbed Fe(II) and tightly-bound Fe(II) (mostly FeCO3 with little FeS) together constituted 26–54% of the reactive iron. The δ56Fe values (−1.97 ± 0.08‰ to −1.49 ± 0.09‰) of sorbed Fe(II) plus tightly-bound Fe(II) were lighter than those at 1–4 cm depth. The isotope fractionation between Fe(III) (oxyhydr)oxides and sorbed Fe(II) plus tightly-bound Fe(II) ranged from 1.56 ± 0.11‰ to 2.31 ± 0.11‰ below 4 cm depth, which was larger than that observed at 1–4 cm depth. Our results show that the iron isotopes in the sediment exhibit distinct fractionation depending on the iron reduction pathways, and offer the first comprehensive iron isotope dataset for abiotic sulfide-driven iron redox cycling acquired directly from temperate eutrophic freshwater lake sediments. The findings provide a framework for comprehending how iron undergoes redox cycling and associated isotope compositions in analogous lacustrine sediments.

title: Early diagenetic dolomitization in methane seep carbonates constrained by coupled Mo and Mg isotopes
description: Publication date: 15 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 427 Author(s): Meng Jin, Zice Jia, Jie Li, Xun Sun, Shaomin Lin, Jörn Peckmann, Qinxian Wang, Duofu Chen, Dong Feng
abstract: Marine carbonates are widely regarded as excellent archives for recording the geochemical evolution of seawater. However, the long-standing “dolomite problem” has hindered the reconstruction of formation mechanisms and depositional settings of the widespread occurrences of dolomite throughout Earth’s history. Cold seeps, where sulfate-driven anaerobic oxidation of methane (SD-AOM) promotes the formation of dolomite, are key to deciphering low-temperature dolomitization processes. Here, we investigate late Miocene to early Pleistocene seep dolomite from Chiahsien, Taiwan, together with modern seep dolomite from the Gulf of Mexico and South China Sea, using a coupled molybdenum (Mo) and magnesium (Mg) isotope approach to constrain the dolomitization environment and processes within seep systems. The wide range of authigenic Mo isotope compositions (δ98Moauth: 0.29 to 2.94‰), correlating with Fe/Al ratios, tracks changes of methane flux spanning from diffusion-dominated (enrichment of heavy Mo) to oxide-shuttle-dominated (enrichment of light Mo) regimes. This contrasts with the homogeneous δ26Mg values of seep dolomite (−2.72 ± 0.21‰), reflecting equilibration with seawater during dolomitization in a shallow, porewater environment with high replenishment of seawater Mg. The Chiahsien seep dolomite further displays higher crystallographic ordering expressed as I(015)/I(110), generally lower Sr/(Mg + Ca) ratios, and more euhedral crystals than modern seep dolomite. Taken together, our new observations suggest that precursor carbonate minerals (aragonite, calcite) were dolomitized during early diagenesis at shallow depth. The lack of Rayleigh fractionation effects of Mg isotope distinguishes seep dolomite from dolomite formed in more restricted, deeper settings, such as environments dominated by organic sulfate reduction and methanogenesis. This study demonstrates that combined Mo–Mg isotope systematics can effectively decipher the redox history and the process of dolomitization. Furthermore, it suggests that seep dolomite, which tends to form in open, seawater-buffered porewater environments, is a promising archive for reconstructing the Mg isotope composition of ancient seawater.

title: Variable silicate weathering and enhanced reverse weathering during the Ordovician-Silurian transition
description: Publication date: 15 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 427 Author(s): Xiangrong Yang, Detian Yan, Denglin Han, David J. Wilson, Philip A.E. Pogge von Strandmann, Xianyi Liu, Chun-Yao Liu, Ke Xu, Can Chen, Mu Liu, Daizhao Chen
abstract: The causes of climate change during the Late Ordovician and Early Silurian remain debated. In order to reveal the relationship between climate, continental weathering, and reverse weathering during this interval, this study presents new records of Li isotopes in marine shales (δ7Lishale) from the Wangjiawan section (Global Boundary Stratotype Section and Point for the base of the Hirnantian Stage) and boreholes BD-1 (shallow shelf setting) and YD-1 (deep shelf setting) in South China. The BD-1 borehole shows consistently low δ7Lishale values in the early Rhuddanian (∼ 0 to 5‰). The YD-1 borehole exhibits similar trends to the existing Dob’s Linn section from Scotland, with higher δ7Lishale values in the early Hirnantian (∼ 11‰) than in the late Katian and late Hirnantian-Rhuddanian (∼ 0‰). The high δ7Lishale values during the Hirnantian Glaciation are likely attributed to more incongruent weathering. In contrast, the Wangjiawan (WJW) section is characterised by extremely variable, and often high, δ7Lishale values (−4.2‰ to 18.9‰) throughout the Ordovician-Silurian transition (OST). Given that the maximum values of δ7Lishale fall into the range of reconstructed δ7Liseawater for this interval (16‰ to 23‰), muted isotopic fractionation between marine authigenic clay and seawater (Δmac-seawater = − 8‰) is tentatively inferred, consistent with previous studies. In this case, the high δ7Lishale values were possibly related to enhanced marine authigenic clay formation and/or reverse weathering, caused by the widespread deposition of volcanic ash and the enrichment of biogenic silica on deep-water shelves. From the variability in shale Li isotope compositions across the OST, possible intervals of δ7Liriver evolution are inferred based on Rayleigh model calculations (Pre-glaciation: δ7Liriver ∼ 10‰; Hirnantian Glaciation: δ7Liriver ∼ 26‰, Post-glaciation: δ7Liriver ∼ 10‰). Hence, the variations of global δ7Liseawater values across the OST could be explained predominantly by changes in the riverine dissolved Li fluxes and δ7Liriver values caused by changes in continental weathering intensity on top of a potentially enhanced reverse weathering baseline. High reverse weathering could have contributed to the warm climate in the early Paleozoic, with variable silicate weathering contributing to climate stabilisation. However, more global sections should be explored to better quantify the magnitude of reverse weathering during the OST.

title: Organic matter controls rare earth element hyper-enrichment in Pacific deep-sea bioapatite
description: Publication date: 15 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 427 Author(s): Xijiao Liao, Dengfeng Li, Simon W. Poulton, John R. Reinfelder, David Chew, Yu Fu, Yongjia Liang, Zhengkun Li, Jinzhou Peng, Xiaoming Sun
abstract: Bioapatite is a predominant sink for rare earth elements (REE) in global deep-sea sediments, where the REE accumulate either via organic matter remineralization or Fe–Mn (oxyhydr)oxide dissolution. While the sequestration of REE into bioapatite has been extensively documented, the mechanistic pathways governing REE transfer from these carrier phases to bioapatite during diagenesis remain poorly constrained. This limits understanding of REE hyper-enrichment in deep-sea sediments, and impacts the reliability of REE signatures in bioapatite as palaeoceanographic tracers. In this study, we elucidate the mechanisms of REE hyper-enrichment from marine porewaters into bioapatite in the presence of Fe–Mn (oxyhydr)oxides and organic matter, using a combination of adsorption experiments integrated with micro-X-ray absorption fine structure (μ-XAFS), X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES), and extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) analyses. Results demonstrate that bioapatite can rapidly adsorb REE from a simulated porewater environment (equilibrium time <1 h) via the formation of stable inner-sphere complexes. XANES and EXAFS evidence further reveals that these complexes are strongly coordinated by PO4 3− groups, as exemplified by Y3+ with well-defined coordination shells: Y–O (2.37 Å), Y-P1 (3.50 Å), and Y-P2 (3.71 Å), which maintains long-term REE retention in bioapatite. Furthermore, we show that organic matter regulates REE cycling through coupled direct and indirect pathways: (1) enhancing short-term REE adsorption onto bioapatite through complexation with CO and O–H bonds, accounting for 79–94% of initial REE uptake; and (2) indirectly promoting long-term REE sequestration by driving the reductive dissolution of Fe–Mn (oxyhydr)oxides, which enhances the REE supply to porewaters for subsequent adsorption by bioapatite. We therefore propose that organic matter plays a central role in controlling REE hyper-enrichment by coupling REE sources (organic matter and Fe–Mn (oxyhydr)oxides) with long-term retention in bioapatite during early diagenesis. This explains the spatial variability in REE enrichment observed across Pacific sediments, and establishes a refined framework for evaluating the early diagenetic alteration of REE signatures.

title: Rethinking uranium immobilization under reducing conditions in groundwater: mineral colloids as an overlooked control
description: Publication date: 15 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 427 Author(s): Xiaoyan Wei, Xinyi Shi, Weida Liu, Jiaxing Ban, Bin Ma, Duoqiang Pan, Wangsuo Wu, Sergey V. Churakov
abstract: Reduction-mediated immobilization is widely considered as a reliable strategy for remediation of uranium contaminated sites. However, the potential role of environmental colloids in the efficiency of remediation applications has been overlooked. This study investigates the role of illite colloids (IC) in modulating the environmental behavior of uranium in zero valent iron (ZVI) contained reducing media under varying ionic strengths and flow rates. Through a combination of column transport experiments and spectroscopic analyses, it was demonstrated that IC facilitates uranium transport in reductive media. Uranium transport is dominated by U(VI) species at low ionic strength, whereas U(IV) co-transport becomes increasingly important at high ionic strength. Notably, the contribution of U(IV) to transported uranium increased substantially at low flow rate and high ionic strength. Spectroscopic evidence reveals that IC enhances U(IV) transport through a mechanism driven by U(VI) reduction on IC surface or in solution, rather than on ZVI surface. Fe-mediated redox processes involving IC and ZVI, together with the enhanced stability of IC under anoxic conditions, may facilitate the formation and mobility of U(IV)-associated IC colloids under reducing conditions, particularly at elevated ionic strength. These findings reveal the risk of U(VI)/U(IV) mobilization in the presence of environmental colloids, emphasizing the need to optimize remediation strategies by suppressing colloid-facilitated transport.

title: Geochemical origins and post-emplacement alteration of natural gases in ultra-deep Ediacaran–Cambrian reservoirs, Sichuan Basin
description: Publication date: 15 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 427 Author(s): Ziqi Feng, Chenzhao Quan, Fang Hao, Huayao Zou, Mingxiang Yang, Haohao Wang, Xiang Piao
abstract: Natural gases from deep to ultra-deep Ediacaran–Cambrian carbonate reservoirs in the Sichuan Basin exhibit complex geochemical signatures, including widespread isotope reversals, inconsistent with conventional single-source maturation models. These features reflect the combined effects of multi-source mixing and intense post-emplacement thermal alteration. Integrated geochemical data and quantitative modeling constrained by thermal simulation experiments indicate that the gases are multi-source mixtures in which external oil-cracking gas provides the dominant charge (typically 40–60%), with additional contributions from in situ source rock-derived thermogenic gas. In the most thermally mature reservoirs, extreme isotopic signatures result from intense fluid-mediated alteration, characterized by near-complete ethane cracking (δ13C2 of up to –23.6‰) and hydrogen isotope rollover ( δ 2 H - CH 4 < –155‰) caused by methane-water interaction. Quantitative modeling results further show that diffusive loss, while significant for the gas volume, played a subordinate role in the isotope fractionation. In this study, we established a multi-stage genetic model for these gases, in which an initial mixing event was subsequently overprinted by intense, in situ geochemical reactions.

title: Suppressed upwelling during the Cambrian–Ordovician transition revealed by coupled Cr–Cd isotope systematics
description: Publication date: 15 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 427 Author(s): Guoqiang Luan, Karem Azmy, Robert Frei, Chengyan Lin, Jianli Lin, Guangyou Zhu
abstract: Biodiversity remained at a plateau between the Cambrian Explosion and the Great Ordovician Biodiversification Event, marked by high rates of both extinction and origination. Widespread oceanic anoxia and transgression-driven upwelling of anoxic deep waters have been widely invoked to explain these biotic perturbations, yet how elevated origination rates were sustained under such environmentally stressful conditions remains poorly understood. Here we present coupled chromium (δ53Cr) and cadmium (δ114Cd) isotope data, together with trace-element records, from marine carbonates at the Cambrian–Ordovician Global Stratotype Section and Point (GSSP) at Green Point, eastern Laurentia. Across the transgressive interval, carbonates record a positive δ53Cr excursion, reflecting enhanced internal marine Cr cycling driven by expanded water-column anoxia. In contrast, a negative δ114Cd excursion records a shift in surface-water sourcing rather than increased nutrient supply or primary productivity. Persistently negative Ce anomalies indicate that surface waters remained oxygenated throughout transgression, despite intensified anoxia at depth. Comparison with coeval carbon-isotope records further suggests that upwelling, where present, was restricted to outer-shelf environments and did not significantly impact shallow surface waters. Together, these observations demonstrate that deep-water anoxia expanded during sea-level rise, but its chemical influence was largely decoupled from the surface mixed layer owing to suppressed upwelling. We propose that enhanced water-column stratification under greenhouse climate conditions limited vertical exchange, confining anoxic waters to depth while preserving ventilated and habitable shallow-marine environments. This physical decoupling provides a mechanistic explanation for how high origination rates could be maintained during intervals of recurrent anoxia, facilitating rapid ecological recovery and setting the environmental stage for the Great Ordovician Biodiversification Event.

title: Vanadium isotopes demonstrate depth-dependent magma differentiation in Rindjani Volcano, Sunda arc
description: Publication date: 15 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 427 Author(s): Xin Ding, Min Ji, Weixin Lv, Fang Huang, Erik V. Sørensen, Paul M. Holm, John D. Foden
abstract: The andesitic composition of the continental crust—characterized by high SiO2 and low FeOT contents—has been attributed to differentiation processes operating in arc settings. One contributing mechanism could be amphibole-forming peritectic reaction at the crust–mantle boundary; however, its role in arc magma differentiation remains poorly constrained. Here we present high-precision δ 51/50V data (hereafter δ51V) for volcanic rocks from the Rindjani suite in the Sunda arc that span compositions from high-Al basalts to trachydacites, investigating how V isotopes respond to amphibole-controlled magma differentiation. At the crust–mantle boundary, amphibole-forming peritectic reactions transform H2O-rich magma into Si-rich melt and induce minor δ51V variation of approximately 0.08‰. H2O-rich magmas that bypass the peritectic reaction ascend to the shallow crust and differentiate from high-Al basalts to high-K andesites, showing limited δ51V variation from −0.76‰ to −0.66‰. Shallow-level differentiation of the Si-rich melt from andesites to trachydacites produces a sharp increase in δ51V from −0.62‰ to −0.04‰, consistent with an average mineral-melt fractionation factor Δ51Vmineral–melt ≈ −0.30‰. Published Fe−Ti isotope data show that δ56Fe remained constant, whereas δ49Ti responded to differentiation throughout the compositional range of the Rindjani suite. The decoupled Fe–Ti–V isotope systematics reveal differences in elemental mass balance and mineral–melt isotope fractionation during magma differentiation. These results show that amphibole-forming peritectic reactions fundamentally modify melt chemistry, thereby enabling significant V isotope fractionation associated with magnetite crystallization at shallow levels. Our findings highlight the depth–dependent differentiation framework of arc magmas and advance understanding of the V isotopic pathways involved in continental crust formation.

title: Observational and experimental constraints on iodine cycling in low oxygen waters
description: Publication date: 15 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 427 Author(s): Keyi Cheng, Colleen M. Hansel, Ian Carley, Maren Voss, Michaela A. TerAvest, Matthew O. Schrenk, Dalton S. Hardisty
abstract: Iodine is widely applied as a paleoredox proxy for ancient atmospheric and seawater O2 accumulation because marine iodine is redox sensitive and its dissolved speciation is preserved in carbonate rocks. However, while the oxidized iodate (IO3 -) is observed to become depleted relative to the reduced iodide (I-) in modern and ancient low oxygen settings, the mechanisms and relationship with oxygen, if any, remain unclear. To provide constraints on potential O2 controls on the iodine biogeochemical cycle, we collected depth profiles and investigated iodine cycling in 2 sub-basins of the Baltic Sea (Fårö and Gotland Deep) and performed laboratory IO3 - reduction experiments in cultures of the facultative bacterium Shewanella oneidensis at variable O2 levels. Like other stratified euxinic systems, I- increases and IO3 - declines at or below the chemocline. The Baltic Sea, however, has complex patterns between iodine species that are decoupled from O2, likely reflecting the unique hydrological and biogeochemical conditions of this stratified system. Notably, we observe significant IO3 - depletion in the fully oxygenated surface layers of the Baltic Sea, a phenomenon uncommonly reported elsewhere. Our culture experiments provide evidence that S. oneidensis preferentially reduces O2 over IO3 - until O2 levels are < 0.1 µM, which are only relevant in anoxic and suboxic (nitrogenous and manganous) zones of the Baltic Sea. We suggest that instead of in situ reduction in the sampled surface waters, the depleted surface water IO3 - is a legacy effect of previous hypoxia either within surface waters and/or along the flow path sourcing surface waters. Since I- oxidizes relatively slowly, such legacy effects may reflect past shoaling of the oxycline or be at least partially the result of the frequency since the last Major Baltic Inflow (MBI) (in this case 7 years), which intermittently introduce oxygenated, IO3 --rich seawater from the North Sea. Together, our findings have important implications for secular IO3 - and O2 accumulation throughout Earth history. The microbial reduction experiments provide refined constraints on atmospheric O2 accumulation at the Paleoproterozoic Great Oxidation Event (∼4 × 10-4 of the present atmospheric level, or PAL), when IO3 - initially accumulated. Further, comparison to the Baltic Sea provides evidence that O2 and IO3 - may become decoupled in redox-stratified and restricted basins even after atmospheric O2 increases, which may contribute to observations of widespread muted IO3 - accumulation even throughout the Phanerozoic.

title: Rubidium isotopes reveal no sub-arc melting of altered oceanic crusts in a cold subduction zone
description: Publication date: 15 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 427 Author(s): Zi-Qiang Zhong, Ding-Sheng Jiang, Saskia Erdmann, Yi-Xiang Chen, Xia Hu, Zheng Xu, Wei Zhang, Jia-Ru Sheng, Wang-Ye Li, Fang Huang
abstract: The extent to which partial melting of subducting slabs contributes to arc magmatism beneath sub-arc regions in cold subduction zones remains highly debated. Traditional models emphasize that altered oceanic crust (AOC) undergoes dehydration, while subducted sediments undergo partial melting. However, an increasing number of studies have argued that partial melting of AOC may also be required to account for the trace-element budgets of arc lavas, particularly their elevated Sr concentrations. To investigate whether AOC undergoes partial melting beneath sub-arc regions, we report Rb isotope (δ87Rb) data for the Cretaceous arc basalts and back-arc basalts associated with the cold subduction zone of the Izanagi plate in Eastern China. The δ87Rb values of the basalts show clear variation across the subduction zone, increasing from −0.31 ± 0.45‰ (2SD, N = 9) for the arc basalts to −0.19 ± 0.07‰ (2SD, N = 22) for the back-arc basalts. This across-arc variation in δ87Rb indicates that while partial melting of subducted sediments occurs across the sub-arc and back-arc regions, partial melting of AOC is only evident in the back-arc region, not beneath the sub-arc region. Moreover, negative correlations between δ87Rb and Sr concentrations strongly suggest that the elevated Sr concentrations (385–913 μg/g) of the arc basalts resulted from the subduction input from sediments, rather than AOC melts as has recently been proposed for global data. Similar compositional relations are observed in arc lavas from other cold subduction zones (Izu-Bonin-Mariana and Tonga-Kermadec), which typically exhibit a negative correlation between Sr/Y and 143Nd/144Nd or Nb/U ratios. Together with recent δ87Rb data from the Mariana arc, our results indicate that in cold subduction zones, AOC may not necessarily undergo partial melting beneath the sub-arc region—even though subducted sediments do. Partial melts of metasomatic pyroxenites formed by interaction between sediment melts and the sub-arc mantle peridotites can carry a significant budget of trace elements, including Sr, contributing to arc magmas. The lack of partial melting in AOC beneath sub-arc regions permits the deep transport of water, carbon, and trace elements, with significant implications for mantle heterogeneity, carbon flux imbalance, and global geochemical cycling.

title: Elevated silicon content facilitates carbon precipitation within Mercury’s core
description: Publication date: 15 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 427 Author(s): Juliana G. Peckenpaugh, Meryem Berrada, Peng Jiang, Bin Chen
abstract: Mercury’s highly reduced formation conditions likely promoted the incorporation of silicon into its metallic core during planetary differentiation. The resulting Si-rich core composition would reduce the capacity of the metallic liquids to dissolve carbon, making carbon saturation more likely as the core cooled and crystallized. Determining the solubility of carbon in Fe-Si liquids under Mercury’s core conditions is therefore essential for evaluating whether graphite or diamond could precipitate from the core and influence Mercury’s thermal and magnetic evolution. In this study, high-pressure and high-temperature experiments were conducted on carbon-saturated Fe-Si alloys with varying silicon content from 4 to 27 wt% using a multi-anvil press at 5–20 GPa and 1673–1873 K. The analyses of the recovered samples by Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) and Raman spectroscopy show the Fe-Si-C liquids with precipitated carbon phases in the form of graphite or diamond. Quantitative electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) results demonstrate a trend of decreasing carbon content in the Fe-Si-C alloys with increasing silicon content, described by the following equation: CFe-Si = 8.45–0.663[Si] + 0.0134[Si]2 . Higher initial silicon content within Mercury’s core due to the highly reduced conditions may result in lower solubility of carbon, suggesting a potential mechanism for the preferential exsolution of carbon-rich materials, such as graphite or diamonds. This finding suggests that carbon could precipitate within Mercury’s cooling, solidifying core under Mercurian core compositions and conditions. The segregation and accumulation of carbon could modify heat flux across the core-mantle boundary, affecting both the strength of Mercury’s early magnetic field and the longevity of dynamo action. Such compositional convection could sustain a dynamo, contributing to Mercury’s present-day magnetic field.

title: Inclusion evidence for melt-fluid evolution and rare earth element mineralization in deep intrusive carbonatites
description: Publication date: 15 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 427 Author(s): Xueyin Yuan, Qi Li, Xiaochun Li, Yang Yu, John A. Mavrogenes
abstract: Carbonatite-associated Rare Earth Element (REE) deposits have been the primary source of REEs for decades, yet the melt-fluid evolution and REE mineralization processes in these systems remain enigmatic. In this study, we successfully characterize the REE mineralizing liquids from two large carbonatite REE deposits, based on microscopic analyses of primary REE-rich multi-phase inclusions from pegmatitic ore dykes, and acquisition of their homogenization pressure–temperature (P-T) conditions by using a Raman spectrometer and a hydrothermal diamond anvil cell. The inclusions studied here consist mainly of sulfate, carbonate and REE daughter minerals (65 – 75 vol%), along with subordinate aqueous liquid (20 – 30 vol%) and vapor (<5 vol%). Their homogenization P-T conditions reach 470 – 600 °C and 5.0 – 7.0 kbar, with sulfate and carbonate concentrations being estimated to exceed 50 wt% and 20 wt%, respectively. By referring to the thermodynamic properties of aqueous-salt systems involving carbonates and sulfates, we conclude that such liquids are neither magmatic nor hydrothermal in the conventional sense, but rather transitional brine-melts, or supercritical fluids formed by complete miscibility between aqueous fluids and salt melts under high P-T conditions. More importantly, the identification of REE daughter minerals (burbankite) in these inclusions, along with their dissolution at 450 – 520 °C during heating, provides direct evidence that such brine-melts have a remarkable capacity in transporting and concentrating REEs, hence shall be responsible for the primary mineralization of REEs in carbonatite systems.

title: Indium diffusion in rhyolitic melts: Implications for In enrichment in magmatic-hydrothermal systems
description: Publication date: Available online 25 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Zewei Zhang, Li Zhang, Renzhi Zhu, Wan-Cai Li, Huaiwei Ni
abstract: Indium, a critical metal primarily recovered as a byproduct from granite-related deposits, requires enrichment exceeding 100 times from magmatic sources to form ore deposits due to its exceptionally low crustal abundance. The In diffusivity in silicate melt is one of the most essential parameters controlling In transport and enrichment efficiency, but has yet to be experimentally determined. This study investigated In diffusion in rhyolitic melts with up to 7.0 wt% H2O at 1073–1873 K and 0.5–1.0 GPa in a piston-cylinder apparatus, employing both diffusion couple and In sheet dissolution techniques. Laser ablation ICP-MS analyses of recovered samples yielded concentration profiles, from which In diffusivities were derived via error function fitting. The In diffusivity was found to increase with elevated temperature and water content but to decrease with pressure. At 1 GPa, In diffusivity in granitic melt can be expressed by the following expression: log D In, 1 GPa = - 8.86 ± 0.69 - 6539 ± 1111 - 432 ± 61 w T where D is the In diffusivity in m2/s, w is the water content in wt%, and T is the temperature in K. The pressure effect over 0.5–1 GPa gives an activation volume of 18.9 cm3/mol for In diffusion. Indium diffusion is sluggish compared to other ore-forming elements, with a diffusivity sequence of D Mo < D In ≈ D Sn ≪ D H2O < D Cu ≈ D Ag. The slow In diffusion in melt hinders the enrichment degree of In in the fluid phase to reach the thermodynamic equilibrium prediction. Given the striking similarity in diffusivities of In and Sn in rhyolitic melts, the enrichment ratio of In to Sn in the fluid falls within a narrow range, regardless of whether equilibrium is reached. This can be used to interpret the coupled enrichment of In and Sn observed in cassiterite-sulfide deposits. Our In diffusivity data are also consistent with the observation in fluid-melt partition experiments.

title: Hematite and siderite nanocrystals in ∼3.48 Ga dresser formation jaspilite: implications for early atmospheric O 2 and CO 2
description: Publication date: Available online 24 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Tianyu Zhou, Huifang Xu, Seungyeol Lee, Eric E. Roden
abstract: Decoding the origin of Precambrian iron formations is essential for evaluating how these rocks record the evolution of early Earth’s surface environment. The ∼ 3.48 Ga jaspilite from Unit A3 of the lower Dresser Formation, Pilbara Craton, Western Australia, provides an exceptional insight to address this challenge based on the intimate association of redox-sensitive Fe(III) oxide (hematite) and Fe(II) carbonate (siderite). This study integrates petrographic observations and geochemical (PHREEQC) modeling to investigate the genesis of hematite and siderite embedded in chert. Nanoscale hematite crystals preserved within hematite-quartz clots formed through ferrihydrite dehydration with limited diagenetic overprinting. Their nanoscale morphology and the absence of relict Fe(II)-silicate (greenalite) precursors support an early authigenic origin rather than secondary oxidation. Two distinct siderite populations in the most Fe-rich jasper layers—partially dissolved crystals left within euhedral micron-scale voids and intact nanoscale rhombs sealed within chert—reflect two different recrystallization stages based on their spatial relationship with hematite-quartz clots. We propose that Dresser Unit A3 jaspilite formed during episodic hydrothermal discharges delivering dissolved Fe-Si, represented by Fe(H3SiO4)2 as a working aqueous metal complex supply, accompanied by abundant seawater/hydrothermal silica input, where comparable rates of Fe(II) oxidation and its combination with dissolved inorganic carbon promoted the simultaneous crystallization of ferrihydrite and siderite, followed by silica gel precipitation. PHREEQC geochemical simulations show that the observed coexistence of siderite and ferrihydrite with plausible Fe-Si source requires CO2-rich conditions (pCO2 ≈ 0.1–0.2 atm) and trace but non-negligible oxygen (pO2 ≈ 10−6 atm), indicating a transient redox state capturing the coprecipitation of Fe(II) and Fe(III) phases. Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ferrihydrite and silica nanoparticles promoted micron-scale colloidal aggregation, later preserved through diagenesis as ∼30 μm hematite–quartz clots. These findings indicate a narrow window of early Archean regional pO2 – pCO2 conditions governing Fe-Si-C-O interplay on Earth’s surface. Our calculated relatively high pO2 level suggests that the Dresser Formation may record one of Earth’s earliest local “whiffs of oxygen” through oxygenic photosynthesis and tectonic oxygen production long before the first major worldwide rise in atmospheric oxygen during the Great Oxidation Event.

title: Particulate manganese shuttling shapes molybdenum and thallium isotope compositions in surface sediments of the Arabian Sea oxygen minimum zone
description: Publication date: Available online 24 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Xinming Chen, Niels A.G. M. van Helmond, Bing Xia, Hainan Lu, Zili Zhao, Yu Zhang, Lulu Wang, Yi-Bo Lin, Feifei Zhang, Gert-Jan Reichart, Caroline P. Slomp
abstract: Sedimentary molybdenum (Mo) and thallium (Tl) isotopes have recently been explored as proxies for reconstructing ocean oxygenation by tracking seafloor manganese (Mn) oxide burial. Although Mn oxides impart the largest isotope fractionations for Mo and Tl in modern oceans and can enhance authigenic accumulation of trace metals (e.g., Mo) in sediments via ‘Mn shuttling’, it remains poorly constrained whether such shuttling affects their isotope compositions in sediments. Here, we measured Mo and Tl isotope compositions in sediments within and below the Arabian Sea oxygen minimum zone (OMZ), where Mn shuttling is occurring. Authigenic Mo isotope compositions (δ98Moauth = 1.70 ± 0.13‰) in ferruginous sediments within the OMZ are similar to those in anoxic but non-sulfidic sediments in modern oceans. In contrast, we observed near-crustal Tl isotope compositions (ε205Tlleach = –1.8 ± 0.5‱) in these sediments, which are different from other modern anoxic sediments. This discrepancy likely results from limited sulfide minerals that host authigenic Tl. Both much lower δ98Moauth and higher ε205Tlleach values (–0.50 ± 0.14‰ and + 2.1 ± 1.1‱) in the Mn-oxide-rich sediments below the OMZ are identical to those of oxic sediments, suggesting a predominant control by particulate Mn shuttling. Post-depositional diagenesis of these sediments leads to a return of Mo and Tl concentrations to crustal levels observed downcore, imposing little effect on global mass balances for Mo and Tl isotopes on longer time spans

title: The underlying mechanism of crop mercury hyperaccumulation in HgS-rich soils: microbially driven enlargement of the bioavailable mercury pool
description: Publication date: Available online 24 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Qingyi Cao, Haiyan Hu, Jen-How Huang, Shirong Liu, Jinquan Chen, Xinbin Feng
abstract: In geological settings rich in mercury sulfide (HgS) minerals, the interaction between microbes and minerals, as a key mechanism driving Hg hyperaccumulation in crops, has long been largely neglected in environmental geochemistry and agricultural research. Microbial sulfur acquisition from HgS minerals for biosynthesis mobilizes Hg(II), concurrently enhancing Hg bioavailability. Under pure culture conditions in LB medium, microbially mediated HgS dissolution and subsequent Hg(II) reduction were correlated with oxidation–reduction potential (ORP). The characteristics of Hg accumulation and distribution in crops are subject to the joint regulation of microbially mediated expansion of the bioavailable Hg pool and the patterns of uptake, translocation, and partitioning within the crop. Mechanistically, microbes secrete cysteine, which converts bulk HgS into bioavailable Hg(II)–cysteine complexes for subsequent crop uptake. Hg isotope analysis (δ202Hg and Δ199Hg) enabled clear source attribution of Hg in the model crop (shallot). The Δ199Hg binary mixing model demonstrated that Hg in roots mainly originated from soil bioavailable Hg pool, whereas leaf Hg originated from both atmosphere and soil. In soil, the Hg extracted by 0.1 M cysteine (2853 ± 740 ng/g) was approximately three orders of magnitude higher than that extracted by 0.1 M HCl (5.53 ± 4.80 ng/g). However, the difference in Δ199Hg between the two extracts was small (only 0.04‰) and fell within the analytical uncertainty. These results indicate that cysteine can effectively mobilize the bioavailable Hg pool in soil, and the isotopic signature of this pool is likely regulated by cysteine‑mediated processes. Microbe–mineral interactions underscore the significant ecological risks posed by microbial activation of HgS in contaminated agricultural soils. Our findings reveal that conventional understanding may lead to substantial underestimation of ecological and health risks at HgS-rich contaminated sites, as well as uncertainties in the management and disposal of HgS-bearing waste.

title: Amorphous carbonates as precursors of dolomite and magnesite in caves
description: Publication date: Available online 24 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Sarah Bonilla-Correa, Encarnación Ruiz-Agudo, Concepción Jiménez de Cisneros, Cristina Liñán Baena, Isabel Sánchez-Almazo, Carlos Rodriguez-Navarro, Maria P. Asta
abstract: Low-temperature (T) dolomite (and magnesite) formation remains a longstanding, strongly debated problem in carbonate geochemistry. It has been recently proposed that protodolomite (at low-T) and ordered dolomite (at high-T) can form via a non-classical route involving an amorphous calcium-magnesium carbonate (ACMC) precursor. Although this crystallization pathway has been observed in the laboratory using abiotic and microbially mediated routes, its occurrence in natural environments has not yet been documented. Here we show the formation of poorly ordered dolomite (protodolomite) and ordered dolomite, along with magnesite, in close association with ACMC and amorphous magnesium carbonate (AMC) in the moonmilk deposits from Nerja Cave (Spain). Our results suggest that these amorphous carbonate phases are crucial precursors in the formation of dolomite and magnesite in this environment, after the initial precipitation of huntite that acts as a Mg2+-rich carbonate reservoir. We show that the crystallization of dolomite and magnesite is governed by a dynamic interplay between fluctuating drip water chemistry, cyclic precipitation-dissolution of huntite, and the stabilization and subsequent crystallization of amorphous carbonate phases mediated by dissolved silica and microbially-derived organic compounds. These findings provide mechanistic insights into low-T dolomite and magnesite formation in cave systems and shed light on their nucleation barrier in Earth’s surface environments.

title: Magmatic-hydrothermal transition and lithium enrichment: Li–B isotope evidence of elbaite for fluid recirculation mechanisms
description: Publication date: Available online 23 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Tao Hong, Yin-Ce Ma, Ming-Guo Zhai, Zhang Zhang, Xing-Wang Xu, He Huang, Jun Gao, Gao-Bin Chu
abstract: The magmatic-hydrothermal transition in rare-metal pegmatites is crucial for understanding mineralizing processes, particularly for strategic resources like lithium and beryllium. Tourmaline, a common mineral in pegmatites, serves as an excellent geochemical tracer for this transition. This study examines the Bailongshan Li pegmatite deposit in the western Kunlun Orogen, northwestern China, through detailed textural and geochemical analyses of elbaite (Elb). By integrating data for major and trace elements and Li–B isotope compositions of Elb, the present study delineates the magmatic-hydrothermal transition and its role in ore formation. Elbaite in the Bailongshan Li pegmatite deposit crystallized progressively from Elb-1 (core, magmatic origin, dark green), through Elb-2 (mantle, late magmatic origin, dark green), to Elb-3 (rim, magmatic-hydrothermal transition origin, light green). Li and B isotopes of Elb show different evolutionary trends from Elb-1 to Elb-3: δ11B increases from Elb-1 to Elb-2, whereas no statistically significant variation is observed from Elb-2 to Elb-3.This pattern is interpreted to reflect fractional crystallization (the resolvable core-to-mantle increase) followed by the re-involvement of an early-exsolved, weakly fractionated hydrothermal fluid that imparts no resolvable δ11B change to Elb-3. In contrast, δ7Li remains stable from Elb-1 to Elb-2 but shows a “V”-shaped variation from the late-crystallized range of Elb-2 to Elb-3. This “V”-shaped δ7Li trend likely records a combination of fractional crystallization, melt-fluid separation, and Li diffusion. Boron isotope modeling indicates ≥80% fractional crystallization during Elb-1 and Elb-2 deposition, while Elb-3 formed from exsolved hydrothermal fluids derived from early melt-fluid separation that are re-involved in the crystallization of lithium-bearing minerals (elbaite) during the magmatic-hydrothermal transition with ∼25% fractional crystallization. Elevated δ7Li values (avg. + 14.1 ‰ to + 14.6 ‰) and an increase in mean Li content of ∼1800 ppm between Elb-2 (avg. 5723 ppm) and Elb-3 (avg. 7513 ppm) might reflect Li isotope diffusion driven by concentration gradients. Reintroduced, weakly fractionated exsolved fluids govern Li mineralization (increasing concentrations of Be, Sn, Ta, and Nb) in elbaite during the magmatic-hydrothermal transition at the Bailongshan Li pegmatite deposit. This study identifies that early-exsolved hydrothermal fluids are re-injected into pegmatitic magmas during pegmatite evolution, a phenomenon conducive to rare metal mineralization. Our work enhances understanding of pegmatite evolution and provides a new mechanistic explanation for pegmatite-hosted rare metal mineralization.

title: Cerium isotope fractionation during adsorption onto mineral surfaces: tracing redox transitions and manganese cycling
description: Publication date: Available online 23 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Yuanyuan Wang, Ryoichi Nakada, Yoshio Takahashi, Yuefei Ding, Wenshuai Li
abstract: Stable cerium (Ce) isotopes have emerged as a promising redox tracer in Earth surface environments, which are also critical for understanding cycling of Mn with a high Ce affinity. Here, we investigated the direction, magnitude, and mechanisms of Ce isotope fractionation during its adsorption onto various clays in a closed system across a range of initial Ce solution concentrations. Lighter isotopes are preferentially adsorbed onto clays, resulting in minor equilibrium isotopic fractionation (αLq-so: 1.000144 ± 0.000007–––1.000208 ± 0.000037) between the solid and liquid phases, regardless of the presence of Ce(IV)-bearing phases such as goethite, or the absence thereof, as in kaolinite, smectite, ferrihydrite, and magnetite. An exception is observed for Ce adsorption on Mn2O3, following a Rayleigh fractionation model (αLq-so: 1.00015), driven by kinetic Ce(III) oxidation and subsequent precipitation. Based on the data compiled from this study and literature, we conclude that the extent of 14⁰Ce enrichment in solids with equilibrium fractionation factors following the order δ-MnO2 (αeq: 1.000411)> > Fe (oxyhydr)oxides (αeq 1.000168) ≈ clay minerals (αeq 1.000153). In contrast, the Mn2O3 system is better described by Rayleigh fractionation, with an effective αRay of 1.00015, reflecting a kinetically controlled, non-equilibrium process. Thus, Ce isotope fractionation may serve as a more robust and complementary tracer for the redox transition from suboxic to oxic conditions, particularly when combined with Ce anomalies and mineralogical context, and provide new insights into Mn cycling in natural environments.

title: Stable isotope evidence for light Zn burial in an oxic coastal bay: Implications for the modern marine Zn budget
description: Publication date: Available online 23 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Yuchen An, Yi Liu, Sheng He, Wei Yuan, Hongming Cai, Wangcai Shuai, Yunchao Lang, Jun Sun, Jiubin Chen
abstract: Understanding zinc (Zn) cycling in coastal environments is crucial for constraining the global marine Zn budget and evaluating its impact on marine ecosystems. Here, we present the first detailed study of Zn isotope systematics across multiple environmental compartments (including surface sediments, sediment cores, riverine sediments, and aerosols) in the Bohai Bay (BHB), a shallow, semi-enclosed, oxic coastal system in northern China. Our results show that sedimentary Zn is derived from two dominant fluvial sources: Yellow River-derived detrital input representing natural lithogenic material and Haihe River particulates carrying an urban anthropogenic signature. By contrast, coastal industrial activities, atmospheric deposition, mariculture, and antifouling paints make only limited direct contributions to sedimentary Zn in BHB. Instead, up to ∼ 60% of sedimentary Zn is authigenic and exhibits an isotopically light signature (δ66Zn value varying from –0.87 to + 0.26‰). Multiple lines of evidences, including covariations in Fe and Zn enrichment factors, microscale mineralogical data, and contrasting Fe vs. Al distribution, indicate that seawater Zn burial is likely dominated by scavenging to reactive Fe-Mn (oxyhydr)oxides under oxic conditions. This interpretation is further supported by offshore core BHB16, which records the highest authigenic Zn fraction and yields the δ66Zn values (δ66Znauth = 0.07 ± 0.28‰, 2SD, n = 37) overlapping those of deep-sea dispersed Fe-Mn (oxyhydr)oxides reported previously (δ66Zn = –0.02‰ to + 0.34‰). Overall, our findings reveal a significant but previously under-constrained sink for isotopically light Zn in the modern marine Zn cycle.

title: Contrasting Mo isotopic signatures in basalts linked to distinct subduction processes in the North China Craton
description: Publication date: Available online 19 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Jian-Fang Guo, Qiang Ma, Liang Ma, Yi-Gang Xu, Jian-Ping Zheng, Chao Zhang, Hao Hu
abstract: Subduction is a fundamental process driving mantle evolution and material recycling, yet distinguishing the contributions of oceanic versus continental subduction to mantle heterogeneity remains a challenge. This study examines Mo isotopes, combined with elemental and Sr-Nd-Pb isotopic data of Early Cretaceous basalts in Sihetun (western Liaoning) and Feixian (western Shandong) in the North China Craton (NCC), regions influenced by distinct subduction processes. Sihetun basalts, exhibit light Mo isotopic compositions (δ 98/95Mo = -0.97 to −0.60‰), low Mo contents (0.32 − 0.41 ppm), high Ce/Mo ratios (292 − 426), and EMI-like Sr-Nd isotopic compositions. These characteristics suggest a mantle source containing dehydrated oceanic crust and pelagic sediments, possibly related to the oceanic subduction of the Paleo-Pacific plate. In contrast, Feixian basalts show heavier Mo isotopic signatures (δ 98/95Mo = -0.09 to 0.07‰), higher Mo contents (1.1 − 1.4 ppm), lower Ce/Mo ratios (137 − 197), and EMII-like Sr-Nd isotopic compositions. These features point to the contribution of recycled continental crust and terrigenous sediments in their mantle sources, suggesting that their sources were affected by both deep subduction of the Yangtze continent and subduction of the Paleo-Pacific plate. These distinct Mo isotopic variations across the NCC reveal that oceanic subduction leads to lighter Mo signatures, while continental subduction introduces heavier Mo isotopic signature to the overlying lithospheric mantle. This study highlights Mo isotopes as a powerful tracer for subduction-related processes and provides new insights into how oceanic and continental subduction regimes drive mantle enrichment and global geochemical cycles

title: The water isotope fractionation coefficient of hydrogen and oxygen in equilibrium with ice and supercooled water at −20°C and the role of supersaturation during ice formation
description: Publication date: Available online 18 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): P.P. Ebner, H.C. Steen-Larsen
abstract: Ice-vapor equilibrium fractionation factors are critical for using water stable isotopes to understand hydrological cycle processes and reconstruct past climate variability. However, significant disagreements in the equilibrium fractionation coefficients among previous works exist. Here, we present an experimental study to reconcile past findings by freezing out water vapor under a controlled environment in a glass flask. This was specifically designed to investigate the effect of supersaturation on the transient behavior of the fractionation coefficient at −20.4°C and to evaluate steady-state assumptions. Two phase transitions (1) vapor-supercooled water and (2) vapor-ice have been analyzed. In addition, a physical model is provided to evaluate the effect of supersaturation on the fractionation coefficient in an equilibrium chamber. The observed results showed transient variability during the experiments and a humidity concentration effect on the apparent fractionation coefficient of the vapor introduced into the equilibrium chamber. Based on the experimental data and model evaluation, the equilibrium fractionation coefficients at −20.4°C for vapor over ice are 1.0202 (±0.0013) for 1H1H18O and 1.1943 (±0.0054) for 1H2H16O. For vapor over supercooled water micro droplets at −20.4°C, the equilibrium fractionation coefficients are 1.0182 (±0.0015) for 1H1H18O and 1.1682 (±0.0097) for 1H2H16O. Our findings suggest that the previously estimated fractionation coefficients are influenced by kinetic processes driven by the humidity concentration gradient across the assumed equilibrium chamber. Therefore, previous works were not carried out under true equilibrium conditions.

title: Authigenic ε Nd offsets driven by sediment–pore water exchange: evidence from the Iberian Margin
description: Publication date: Available online 18 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Sara Campderrós, Leopoldo D. Pena, Jaime Frigola, Luke Skinner, Dimitris Evangelinos, Ester Garcia-Solsona, Eduardo Paredes-Paredes, Albert Català, Isabel Cacho
abstract: Neodymium isotopes (εNd) preserved in authigenic phases are widely used as tracers of water mass provenance and mixing in paleoceanography. However, recent studies have questioned its reliability, as processes occurring at the sediment–seawater interface can introduce a distinct εNd signal into pore waters, potentially altering the signal preserved by authigenic phases. This study investigates whether εNd values recorded in different authigenic phases from the Atlantic Iberian margin reliably reflect the isotopic composition of overlying bottom waters. To this end, we present the first high-resolution core-top εNd dataset from this region, including εNd analysis from foraminiferal Fe-Mn coatings, fish debris, and sediment leachates. These results are compared with εNd values of present-day seawater compositions, detrital sediment fraction, and interface water (water immediately above the seafloor). Our results reveal a consistent offset between seawater εNd and the more positive values recorded in all authigenic phases. Interface waters also exhibit more positive εNd signatures, suggesting that a reactive sedimentary phase that constitutes a minor component of the sediment, with a more positive εNd dissolves into pore water. Consequently, both the isotopic composition recorded by authigenic phases and that of the seawater immediately above the seafloor are also modified to more positive εNd values. Differences between the εNd signal recorded by foraminifera coatings, fish debris, and sediment leachates further suggest that εNd is incorporated through phase-specific diagenetic and geochemical processes. We also investigate how changing redox conditions in the sediment column affect the εNd signal recorded by foraminifera. Despite early diagenetic remobilization of Fe–Mn coatings evidenced by changes in U/Mn ratios measured in foraminiferal coatings, εNd values remain consistent downcore, suggesting that redox conditions do not substantially modify the εNd ratios. Altogether, our results suggest the presence of a reactive sedimentary phase that modifies pore water εNd. This altered signal is subsequently transferred to the authigenic phases, thereby compromising the reliability of εNd as tracer of past water mass provenance in the studied margin.

title: The evolution, migration, and transformation of dissolved organic matter in black shale regions: environmental destination and implications
description: Publication date: Available online 17 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Yinbo Xu, Guangxu Zhu, Pei Xu, Changqiu Zhao, Rongfei Wei, Usman Kaku Dawuda, Qingjun Guo
abstract: The weathering of black shales represents a critical yet poorly constrained pathway of petrogenic organic carbon release into the modern carbon cycle. Despite its potential importance, the molecular-level processes governing the fate of this ancient dissolved organic matter (DOM) remain elusive. In this study, integrated optical, ultra-high-resolution mass spectrometry (FT-ICR-MS), and thermodynamic analyses were employed to track the compositional shifts of shale-derived DOM across a spatially linked rock-soil–water continuum. Results reveal that the mobilized rock DOM exhibits an unexpected dual nature. While the pool is overwhelmingly dominated by formulas in the “lignin-like” stoichiometric space (∼64%, likely representing carboxyl-rich alicyclic molecules or oxidized kerogen fragments rather than vascular plant residues), it simultaneously releases bio-labile, aliphatic-rich signatures. Molecular network analysis unveils an active, bidirectional transformation hub centered around these moderately oxidized intermediate structures, demonstrating that petrogenic carbon is dynamically repackaged rather than entirely refractory. Although DOM oxidation is thermodynamically favorable across all media (ΔGcox ≈ −118 to −124 kJ/mol-C), distinct environmental filters dictate its fate. The relative enrichment of aliphatic/lipid-like formulas in the aquatic system (from 4.7% to 9.7%) is driven by in-situ microbial production and constrained by thermodynamic efficiency. Specifically, lower maximum energy transfer efficiencies (λ ≈ 0.041) in the stream limit the metabolic reward for microbial degradation, promoting the relative persistence of these aliphatic compounds. Conversely, highly oxygenated aromatic signatures (“tannin-like”) decline sharply (from 11.1% to 2.3%) due to preferential mineral sorption and microbial humification within the soil layer. Our findings suggest that the fate of petrogenic carbon undergoes complex molecular recycling—characterized by aliphatic mobilization, aromatic soil filtration, and aquatic biogenic reshaping. This dynamic view resolves the paradox of its apparent persistence and continuous molecular renewal, providing a mechanistic molecular framework for understanding the activation and fate of petrogenic carbon within the modern critical zone

title: Chlorine isotope compositions of the southern Tibetan lithosphere indicate a mantle source for chlorine in collisional porphyry Cu systems
description: Publication date: Available online 15 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Qiushi Zhou, Rui Wang, Chetan Nathwani, Heejin Jeon
abstract: The India-Asia convergence generated a series of porphyry deposits formed in the post-collisional stage, yet the enrichment mechanisms of critical ore-forming elements such as chlorine (Cl) remain poorly understood. Multi-isotope systems, particularly Cl isotopes, offer a powerful tool to trace these material cycling processes. However, the limited understanding of the δ37Cl values of collisional zones has hindered our understanding of Cl cycling. To address this, we systematically collected ore-forming porphyries, granitoid batholiths, a deep crustal granulite xenolith, an ultramafic cumulate, and an ultrapotassic volcanic rock from the southern Tibetan Plateau. Apatite Cl and Nd isotopes, along with whole-rock boron (B) isotopes, were analyzed to constrain the Cl isotope compositions of various endmembers and to further trace the origin of Cl for porphyry ore-forming magmas. From the Late Cretaceous to the Oligocene, the Zedong granitoid batholiths exhibit progressively enriched apatite εNd(t) and decreasing apatite δ37Cl, indicating increasing involvement of a low-δ37Cl enriched crustal component. Two components are therefore recognized in the collisional crust: a juvenile, depleted crust with high δ37Cl (+0.62 ± 0.28 ‰), and a reworked, enriched crust with relatively low δ37Cl (−0.51 ‰). The post-collisional Qulong and Jiama porphyry deposits show significantly higher apatite δ37Cl values (Qulong: +0.88 ± 0.42 ‰; Jiama: +0.72 ± 0.61 ‰) compared to the Zedong granitoid batholiths (+0.11 ± 0.44 ‰), yet similar to those of ultrapotassic magmas (+0.85 ± 0.10 ‰) and the juvenile crust (+0.88 ± 0.46 ‰). Combined with Nd isotope evidence, we suggest that metasomatized lithospheric mantle (represented by the ultrapotassic magmas) and juvenile crustal components are the dominant sources of Cl in the collisional porphyry ore-forming magmas.

title: The solubility of Nd(OH) 3 (s) and thermodynamic optimization of Nd hydroxyl species in hydrothermal aqueous solutions from 25 to 300 °C
description: Publication date: Available online 14 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Yerko Figueroa Penarrieta, Alexander P. Gysi
abstract: The mobilization of rare earth elements (REE) is controlled in many geological systems by the transport in hydrothermal aqueous fluids. Geochemical models are needed to predict their subsurface behavior and speciation in high temperature and pressure fluids. The REE3+ and REE hydroxyl complexes are known to control the solubility of REE in a wide pH range. However, thermodynamic data for the REE hydroxyl complexes are scarce at hydrothermal conditions. In this study, we measured the solubility of Nd(OH)3(s) between 100 and 250 °C at acidic to mildly acidic pH using batch-type solubility experiments. These data were used in combination with new calorimetric data for the Nd3+ aqua ion and previous potentiometric measurements of Nd hydroxyl species from the literature to optimize the standard partial molal Gibbs energy of formation (Δf G°) and the cumulative formation constants (log β1-3) of Nd hydroxyl complexes using the GEMSFITS code package. The formation constants (Nd3+ + nOH– ⇌ Nd(OH)n 3-n, n = 1 to 3) are fitted together with available literature data as a function of temperature (T) in Kelvin between 25 and 300 °C: log β 1 = -46.38 + 0.06681·T + 9620/T; log β 2 = -50.62 + 0.08554·T + 1074/T; log β 3 = –23.92 + 0.05953·T + 6480/T. These thermodynamic data are implemented in the MINES database and the GEMS code package to model the speciation of Nd as a function of pH and the solubility of monazite in hydrothermal fluids. Differences of up to 2 orders of magnitude are observed between the models generated from the revised thermodynamic data and the calculated predictions based on the Helgeson-Kirkham-Flowers equation of state parameters for REE hydroxyl complexes. The optimized thermodynamic properties improve the modeling of Nd speciation and REE mineral solubility

title: Two stages of Sn enrichment in granitic magmatism: insights from Sn isotopes of cogenetic minerals
description: Publication date: Available online 14 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Jia-Xin She, Weiqiang Li, Ru-Cheng Wang, Lei Xie, Chen Liu, Zhihao Xu, Shichao An, Cheng Xu
abstract: The enrichment of tin (Sn) in high-silica (high-Si) granites is commonly linked to magmatic-hydrothermal processes, yet the respective roles of mineral crystallization versus fluid activity remain debated. Direct constraints on how individual minerals partition Sn and fractionate Sn isotopes during granite differentiation are particularly scarce. Here we report Sn concentrations and stable Sn isotope compositions (δ 122/118Sn3161a) for cogenetic minerals (spodumene, tourmaline, muscovite, biotite, feldspar, quartz, and cassiterite) and whole rocks from the compositionally zoned Pusila leucogranite pluton in the Himalaya. Tin is heterogeneously distributed among minerals: muscovite acts as the principal host and is isotopically heavier than the host rocks, whereas feldspar and quartz contain only minor Sn and are generally isotopically lighter. Cassiterite from pegmatites is also isotopically light, with a mean δ 122/118Sn3161a of 0.036‰. Whole‑rock δ 122/118Sn3161a values increase systematically from −0.035‰ in biotite granite to + 0.337‰ in albite granite, whereas pegmatites show larger Sn isotope variations (0.292‰ to 0.816‰). These observations reveal two distinct stages of Sn behavior. During the magmatic stage, progressive crystallization of feldspar preferentially removes light Sn isotopes from the melt, driving the residual magma toward heavier isotopic compositions while allowing Sn to behave incompatibly. In the pegmatite stage, low Nb/Ta, Zr/Hf, and K/Rb ratios, pronounced REE tetrad effects, and widespread sericitization indicate significant fluid activity. An exsolved Sn-bearing aqueous fluid precipitates isotopically light cassiterite in the pegmatites, leaving the residual melt isotopically heavier. Together, these results support a model in which Sn enrichment involves early magmatic pre‑concentration followed by fluid‑mediated redistribution and cassiterite precipitation. Our findings delineate the mechanisms of Sn enrichment in evolved granitic systems and demonstrate the potential of Sn isotopes as a tracer of magmatic-hydrothermal processes.

title: First-principle study of mineral-solution equilibrium isotope fractionations of magnesium, sulfate and calcium in CaCO 3
description: Publication date: Available online 14 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Chirantan Pramanik, Itay Halevy
abstract: Chemical impurities in CaCO 3 minerals, present as ion substitutions (e.g., Mg 2 + -for-Ca 2 + , SO 4 2 − -for-CO 3 2 − ) are common. Impurities incorporated into a carbonate lattice have a different physicochemical environment than their aqueous forms, resulting in isotopic fractionations of these impurity atoms between the mineral and its parent fluid. Moreover, the lattice distortion in the presence of impurities is proportional to the impurity concentrations, potentially leading to a concentration-dependent effect on the mineral-fluid isotopic fractionation of the impurities and the major elements in the minerals. A mechanistic understanding of the effects of impurities in CaCO 3 minerals on the mineral lattice and the isotopic fractionation of the impurities and major elements is necessary for the use of carbonate minerals and their trace elements as paleo-environmental archives. The difficulty in achieving isotopic equilibrium during experimental precipitation of carbonate minerals motivates the calculation of equilibrium isotope effects by ab initio density functional theory (DFT) methods. However, the utility of DFT calculations in constraining the effects of impurity elements in carbonate minerals on the isotopic fractionation of both the impurities themselves and the major elements in the mineral is limited by computational feasibility. Even a single substitution in a model lattice, composed of as many atoms as computationally feasible for DFT calculations, results in impurity concentrations that are higher than those typical of most natural and experimental samples. Using DFT, we systematically modeled a range of calcite and aragonite supercell sizes with a single Mg or carbonate-associated sulfate (CAS) impurity, allowing calculation of the dependence of the CaCO 3 -fluid isotopic fractionation on the impurity concentration. We studied the change in the impurity bonding environment and computed phonon frequencies to calculate the reduced partition function ratios and the fractionation of S, Mg and Ca isotopes between the CaCO 3 and its parent fluid. We obtained a near-constant CAS-aqueous SO 4 2 − S isotope fractionation in calcite of 2.9‰ over a range of CAS concentrations between 26400 and 58600 ppm (sulfate mole fractions of 1/36 and 1/16), in close agreement with the highest-CAS experimental value of 2.9‰. We found a constant mineral-aqueous Mg 2 + Mg isotope fractionation over the range of modeled impurity concentrations of ∼ –8.6‰ in calcite and ∼ –7.2 to –8.8‰ in aragonite, in agreement with previous computational studies with similar Mg concentrations. We find a difference of up to ∼ 2.1‰ in 1000ln 44 α calcite and 1000ln 44 α aragonite between pure calcite and aragonite supercells and supercells of those minerals with 1/24 and 1/32 mole fractions of sulfate, respectively. A difference of up to ∼ 1‰ of 1000ln 44 α calcite and 1000ln 44 α aragonite from pure calcite and aragonite is observed with similar mole fractions of magnesium.
